Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with 15 ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, 3 g oregano, 3 g paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Cut bell peppers into thick 2 cm strips. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, remaining 1 minced garlic clove, 2 g oregano, 2 g paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread bell peppers on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Peppers should be tender with slight charring.
While peppers roast, heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to skillet. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 15 ml olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, toss salad greens with half of the dressing.
Arrange roasted bell peppers and seared chicken chunks on individual plates.
Place dressed salad greens alongside the chicken and peppers.
Garnish with crumbled feta cheese, chopped fresh parsley, lemon zest, and Kalamata olives.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.
For extra flavor, marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, before cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Bake
recipes.visual_description: Diced chicken pieces and bright green broccoli florets are nestled within a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. The dish is topped with a generous layer of melted, golden-brown cheddar cheese, showing bubbly, slightly crisped edges. The texture is hearty, with tender chicken, slightly firm broccoli, and a smooth, thick sauce beneath a savory cheese crust. Presented as a generous, natural portion scooped into a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin and a metal fork rest beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the comforting appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain white rice or egg noodles to soak up the creamy sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm diced pieces. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Steam broccoli florets for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in plain flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in sour cream until well combined. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked chicken and steamed broccoli to the sauce. Stir gently to coat.
Pour mixture into a 2-liter baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for a few minutes before serving.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to your preference, adding more salt or pepper as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Chicken with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kung Pao Chicken is presented in a traditional white porcelain Chinese bowl, mounded neatly. The dish features tender, succulent cubes of chicken, vibrant red and green bell pepper pieces, and crunchy roasted peanuts. Dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns are visible, adding visual interest and authentic character. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, reddish-brown sauce that glistens under natural, even light. Freshly chopped green scallions are sprinkled generously over the top, providing a pop of color. The bowl is placed on a simple wooden table surface. Beside it, a small white rice bowl holds perfectly steamed white rice. A few crisp, fresh romaine lettuce leaves are arranged neatly to the side, ready for optional wraps. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the rice bowl. The setting is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle, casual bistro-style background, allowing the dish to be the focal point while honoring its cultural presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice as a staple accompaniment.
Offer fresh romaine lettuce leaves for making lettuce wraps.
Serve family-style with chopsticks for communal dining.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Place in a bowl.
Add 5 ml Shaoxing wine, 5 ml light soy sauce, 5 g cornstarch, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of white pepper to chicken. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes to marinate (velvet).
Dice red and green bell peppers into 2 cm pieces.
Mince garlic and ginger. Cut scallions into 2 cm pieces, separating white and green parts.
In a small bowl, combine remaining light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, Chinkiang vinegar, sugar, 10 ml cornstarch, and sesame oil. Mix well to create the sauce.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to the wok. Stir-fry until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned, about 4-5 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Reduce heat to medium-high.
Add dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and chilies darken slightly. Be careful not to burn.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and white parts of scallions. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Stir quickly to combine.
Stir the prepared sauce mixture again. Pour sauce over chicken and vegetables. Stir constantly until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients, about 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in roasted peanuts and green parts of scallions.
Wash and dry romaine lettuce leaves. Serve Kung Pao Chicken immediately with steamed rice and romaine lettuce leaves on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Beef Shepherd's Pie rests on an everyday ceramic plate, set on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The pie features a golden-brown, fork-ridged mashed potato topping, with patches of deeper caramelization. Beneath, the rich, savory beef mincemeat filling, studded with diced carrots and wilted spinach, is visible. The beef is finely broken and simmered to a deep, earthy brown. Colors are warm: golden potatoes, deep brown meat, hints of green and orange. The texture contrasts creamy potato with hearty, saucy filling. The plate is casually placed. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a metal fork are beside it. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the scene. The background suggests a lived-in kitchen, adding to the homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with green peas or steamed green beans on the side.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef mincemeat. Brown thoroughly, breaking up clumps. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and carrot to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in diced tomato and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir in fresh spinach until wilted. Season with salt and pepper.
While filling simmers, mash drained potatoes. Add milk and butter. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Pour beef filling into a 2-liter ovenproof dish if not using an oven-safe pan. Top evenly with mashed potato. Create ridges with a fork.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Pork Donburi with Savory Mayonnaise
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of Simple Pork Donburi with Savory Mayonnaise rests in a deep, dark ceramic donburi bowl on a well-worn wooden dining table. The base is a generous bed of fluffy, pristine white Japanese short-grain rice. Layered on top is a comforting mound of thinly sliced pork shoulder, stir-fried to a tender, slightly caramelized finish with translucent slivers of onion, all coated in a rich, glossy ginger-soy sauce. A delicate, pale yellow drizzle of creamy mayonnaise sauce zigzags across the pork, creating a visual contrast. Bright green, thinly sliced green onions are scattered casually over the top, adding a fresh pop of color and texture. To the side, a small, rustic ceramic dish holds a small portion of vibrant pink pickled ginger. A pair of wooden chopsticks rests naturally on a simple ceramic chopstick rest next to the bowl. A casually folded, slightly wrinkled cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with subtle background clutter. The entire plate is visible, showcasing natural portions and an organic arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of pickled ginger (gari).
Serve with a bowl of miso soup.
Eat with chopsticks.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice according to package directions.
Prepare shogayaki sauce: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, grated ginger, and sugar. Mix well.
Prepare creamy mayonnaise sauce: In another small bowl, whisk together Japanese mayonnaise and water until smooth and slightly pourable.
Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add sliced onion. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add thinly sliced pork to the pan. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until pork is cooked through and lightly browned.
Pour the shogayaki sauce over the pork and onions. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the pork.
Divide cooked rice among 4 individual donburi bowls.
Spoon the cooked pork and onion mixture over the rice in each bowl.
Drizzle the creamy mayonnaise sauce generously over the pork in each bowl.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Schnitzel
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pork schnitzel, irregularly shaped, is centered on a round, plain ceramic plate. Its crispy, textured breading shows distinct golden hues. Adjacent, a modest scoop of creamy mashed potatoes, lightly flecked with chopped fresh parsley, provides a soft contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests casually beside the schnitzel, ready for squeezing. The overall color palette is warm and inviting. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, reflecting warm, natural light from above. A simple, folded linen napkin is placed to the side. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment, with minimal clutter, emphasizing homely comfort and simple, authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh lemon wedge for squeezing over the schnitzel.
Traditionally accompanied by potato salad, mashed potatoes, or boiled potatoes.
instructions: Trim any excess fat from pork cutlets. Place each cutlet between two sheets of plastic wrap.
Pound each cutlet with a meat mallet until approximately 5mm thick. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Prepare breading station: Place flour on a shallow plate. Whisk eggs in a second shallow plate. Place breadcrumbs on a third shallow plate.
Dredge each pork cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, ensuring full coating. Let excess egg drip off.
Coat cutlet thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere. Set aside on a clean plate.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed frying pan over medium-high heat. Oil should be about 1-2 cm deep and reach 170°C.
Carefully place 1-2 schnitzels in the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove fried schnitzels from pan. Place on a wire rack over paper towels to drain excess oil.
Repeat with remaining schnitzels.
Chop fresh parsley finely. Boil or mash potatoes until tender. Serve schnitzels immediately with lemon wedges and a side of potatoes, garnished with parsley.
notes: Pounding the pork thin ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Do not overcrowd the pan; fry schnitzels in batches to maintain oil temperature and achieve crispiness.
For best results, use fresh breadcrumbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken and Tomato Pasta is presented on a modest, everyday ceramic plate. The dish features chunky, cooked chicken pieces, mixed with penne pasta coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. Vibrant green spinach leaves are visible throughout, along with earthy brown mushroom slices and tender diced onion. The ingredients are naturally mixed, forming a hearty, comforting mound in the center of the plate, with some sauce and pasta spilling gently to the edges. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware are casually placed nearby, suggesting a relaxed, family meal setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried basil, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted.
Add cooked pasta to the pot. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Transfer mixture to a 3-liter baking dish if not using an oven-safe pot.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until bubbling and heated through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Stuffed Bell Pepper Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous, comforting portion of Simple Stuffed Bell Pepper Soup. The hearty soup features a rich, reddish-brown broth, studded with tender, browned ground beef crumbles, vibrant diced bell peppers in red, yellow, and green, and soft white rice grains. The ingredients are naturally distributed, creating an inviting, unpretentious appearance. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, reflecting warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple, cream-colored linen napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The setting evokes a homely, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with minimal, unobtrusive background elements. The entire single portion is clearly visible, showcasing its inviting texture and natural colors, ready for a comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned and no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in diced bell peppers. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add diced tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, uncooked rice, and dried oregano. Stir well.
Bring the soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent rice from sticking.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Braised Beef with Bell Peppers and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty braised beef and vegetables is presented on a simple, rustic white ceramic plate, resting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The generously sized beef chunks, cooked to fork-tender perfection, are nestled amidst soft, vibrant red and green bell pepper strips and earthy halved cremini mushrooms, all coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown tomato and herb sauce. The natural arrangement shows the ingredients slightly overlapping. Alongside, a modest pile of golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with slightly crispy edges and soft interiors, is casually placed. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered over the beef for a touch of green. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting colors. A simple, folded linen napkin and basic metal cutlery complete the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss potato wedges with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden and tender. Set aside.
Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge beef lightly in flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, bell pepper strips, and halved mushrooms. Cook for 7-8 minutes until vegetables start to soften.
Stir in tomato paste, dried oregano, dried basil, and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef broth and crushed tomatoes. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Just before serving, stir in the pitted and halved Kalamata olives.
Serve hearty braised beef and vegetables immediately with the roasted potato wedges. Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi with Roasted Bell Pepper Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown potato gnocchi is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The gnocchi are irregularly shaped, each with subtle ridges, and are evenly coated in a vibrant, creamy orange-red roasted bell pepper sauce. The sauce has a smooth, rich texture, pooling slightly at the bottom of the bowl. Scattered over the gnocchi are rough, irregular pieces of golden-brown toasted cashews, adding a textural contrast. A few fresh, deep green basil leaves are artfully placed on top for a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a silver fork rests on a white cotton napkin. A small side plate holds a neat pile of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting, and professional bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta or focaccia bread for dipping in the sauce.
A glass of crisp Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino, pairs well.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skins blister and char.
Remove peppers from oven. Place in a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap for 15 minutes. Peel skins off. Discard skins. Roughly chop roasted bell peppers.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chopped bell peppers and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Transfer bell pepper mixture to a blender. Add cream cheese and maple syrup. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper. Set aside.
For gnocchi: Boil potatoes in their skins until very tender, about 30-40 minutes. Drain potatoes. Peel while hot. Pass through a potato ricer onto a clean work surface.
Spread riced potato to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Form a well in the center. Add flour, egg yolk, and 5 g salt.
Gently mix ingredients with a fork, then knead lightly until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix. Dough should be slightly sticky.
Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, about 2 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces.
Optionally, roll each piece lightly over a gnocchi board or fork tines to create ridges. Place gnocchi on a lightly floured tray.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Drop gnocchi into boiling water in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown. Roughly chop.
Add cooked gnocchi directly to the bell pepper cream sauce. Gently toss to coat. Reheat sauce over low heat if needed.
Serve gnocchi immediately. Garnish with toasted cashews and fresh basil leaves. Serve with a side of mixed salad greens.
notes: Do not overwork the gnocchi dough; it will become tough.
Adjust sauce consistency with a splash of vegetable broth if too thick.
The maple syrup subtly balances the roasted pepper sweetness without making the dish overtly sweet.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato and Kale Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a large, rustic ceramic bowl, suitable for a family meal. Roasted sweet potato cubes, with their slightly browned edges and vibrant orange hue, are scattered throughout the deep green, softened kale. Interspersed among these are creamy white chickpeas, thinly sliced crimson red onion, and bright red cherry tomato halves. A generous drizzle of creamy, pale tan tahini dressing lightly coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, appealing texture. The vegetables are chopped and sliced, not whole, ensuring an easy-to-eat, integrated mix. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, perhaps with a casually placed cloth napkin and simple, everyday flatware. Natural, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the wholesome, inviting nature of the dish.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss diced sweet potato with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast sweet potato for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized. Let cool slightly.
Place chopped kale in a large bowl. Drizzle with 5 ml olive oil. Massage kale with hands for 2-3 minutes until softened.
In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, maple syrup, 40 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Gradually whisk in water until dressing reaches desired consistency.
Add roasted sweet potato, rinsed chickpeas, thinly sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes to the bowl with kale.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately or let sit for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beer-Braised Chicken with Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Belgian Beer-Braised Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs, deeply braised to tenderness, rest centrally on the plate. The chicken is coated in a rich, dark amber sauce that pools around the pieces, glossy and inviting. The sauce contains soft, caramelized onion slices. Bright green, roughly chopped fresh basil leaves are generously sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, providing a vibrant color contrast. A few whole basil leaves garnish the edge of the plate. The composition is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin neatly folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with classic Belgian frites (fries) in a separate paper cone.
Serve with creamy mashed potatoes.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil leaves
ingredients.quantity: 30g, roughly chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until softened and caramelized.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and brown sugar. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in Belgian beer. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze, incorporating all browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Pour in chicken stock. Liquid should partially cover chicken.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover pot.
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken. Skim excess fat from sauce if desired.
Stir in chopped fresh basil into the sauce. Simmer sauce for 5 minutes to slightly reduce and thicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Return chicken to sauce to coat before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A modest, homely single portion of Cheesy Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet rests on a simple, slightly worn ceramic plate, centered on a rustic wooden dining table. The dish presents a comforting blend of textures and colors: tender, diced chicken chunks are nestled within fluffy, savory long-grain white rice, studded with vibrant yellow corn kernels and bits of red diced tomato. A generous layer of golden, melted Monterey Jack cheese blankets the top, with bright green, sliced pickled jalapenos scattered over for a pop of color and a hint of tang. The components touch and slightly overlap, creating a natural, unpretentious arrangement. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro adds a final touch. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen lighting, hinting at a cozy family meal. The background is minimal, reinforcing the authentic, casual home dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer lime wedges for squeezing.
A small bowl of salsa verde or pico de gallo can be offered alongside.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, diced into 2.5 cm cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice, diced tomatoes (undrained), corn kernels, and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return browned chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in half of the shredded cheese until melted and combined.
Sprinkle remaining cheese and pickled jalapeno slices over the top. Cover for 2-3 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Turkey and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Turkey and Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick chunks of golden-brown roasted turkey thighs are nestled among crisp-tender potato wedges, vibrant roasted red and yellow bell pepper strips, and burst cherry tomatoes. Scattered throughout are dark Kalamata olives and thinly sliced red onion. A light drizzle of olive oil enhances the sheen. The dish is garnished generously with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge placed beside the roasted elements. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against a subtly blurred casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Offer a side of simple green salad with a lemon-herb vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red), cut into wedges
Red bell pepper, cut into thick strips
Yellow bell pepper, cut into thick strips
Red onion, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut turkey thighs into thick chunks. Pat dry.
In a large bowl, combine turkey, potato wedges, bell pepper strips, red onion wedges, cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread the mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 30 minutes.

Stir the mixture. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until turkey reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized. Potatoes should be golden and crisp-tender.
Remove from oven. Stir in fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, do not overcrowd the baking sheet. Use two sheets if necessary to ensure even roasting and browning.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Beet and Pickled Egg Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, featuring ample white space. A vibrant bed of mixed local greens forms the base. Ruby red and golden diced roasted beets are scattered artfully, contrasting with the greens. Thin, pale pink slices of pickled red onion are interspersed. Half or quartered pickled eggs, with distinct yellow yolks and firm whites, are nestled among the vegetables. A light, glistening vinaigrette coats the ingredients. Toasted pumpkin seeds are sprinkled for crunch. Fresh dill or parsley sprigs act as a natural garnish. The composition is clean, organic, and unforced, emphasizing the natural beauty and colors of each ingredient. The setting includes a light reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural lighting.

ingredients.name: mixed beets (red, golden, chioggia), peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Prepare Pickled Eggs: Hard boil eggs. Cool and peel. Combine 240 ml apple cider vinegar, 240 ml water, 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, and pickling spice in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer until sugar and salt dissolve. Cool completely. Place peeled eggs in a clean jar. Pour cooled pickling liquid over eggs. Seal and refrigerate for at least 24 hours. Slice eggs in half or quarters before serving.

Roast Beets: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced beets with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.

Prepare Pickled Red Onion: Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml apple cider vinegar, 120 ml water, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil. Pour hot liquid over onions. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Make Dressing: Whisk together 60 ml extra virgin olive oil, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, 1/2 teaspoon maple syrup (if using), salt, and pepper in a small bowl.

Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, roasted beets, and pickled red onion. Add dressing. Toss gently to coat. Divide salad among four plates. Arrange sliced pickled eggs on top. Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh dill or parsley.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing pickling liquids for flavor and preserving ingredients for longer shelf life.
Prioritize seasonal and local produce for the freshest flavor and reduced environmental impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Salami and Sun-Dried Tomato Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Salami and Sun-Dried Tomato Tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The golden tagliatelle is twirled into a neat, elevated mound in the center, coated generously with a creamy, light orange-hued sauce. Visible within the pasta are savory, browned chunks of salami, crispy bits of diced bacon, vibrant deep red pieces of chopped sun-dried tomatoes, and dark, glossy halved Kalamata olives. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, with a few fresh green parsley leaves scattered for a pop of color. The dish is centrally composed, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Traditional Italian flatware accompanies the dish. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Cook tagliatelle pasta according to package directions. Reserve 250 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Cut salami into 1 cm chunks.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic.
Drain sun-dried tomatoes, chop roughly. Halve Kalamata olives.
Grate Parmesan cheese.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Leave rendered fat in skillet.
Add salami chunks to the skillet. Cook until lightly browned. Remove salami with a slotted spoon. Keep a small amount of fat in the pan.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in heavy cream and 100 ml reserved pasta water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the skillet. Add crispy bacon and salami chunks. Toss to coat pasta evenly.
Add halved olives and half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Toss again. If sauce is too thick, add more reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve pasta immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining Parmesan and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Pineapple-Ginger Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Pineapple-Ginger Glaze is presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate, centered on a light wooden table. Two thick, oval-shaped duck medallions, showcasing crisp, golden-brown skin and tender, rosy interior, are arranged side-by-side. A generous, glossy pool of vibrant orange-yellow pineapple-ginger glaze surrounds the duck, with small, soft cubes of pineapple and apple visible within. Toasted almond slivers add textural contrast over the duck and glaze. A small sprig of fresh green thyme is placed beside the duck for color. The background features a blurred, casual bistro setting, with natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The presentation is professional, clean, and inviting, highlighting the dish's rich colors and textures.
instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe pan over medium-low heat. Place duck breasts skin-side down. Render fat slowly for 10-12 minutes until skin is golden brown and crisp.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh-side for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 6-8 minutes until internal temperature reaches 60-63°C (140-145°F) for medium-rare duck.
Remove duck from pan. Let rest on a cutting board, skin-side up, for 5-10 minutes. Reserve rendered duck fat.
For the glaze: Pour off most duck fat from pan, leaving 15ml. Add minced shallot to pan. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add diced pineapple, diced apple, grated ginger, honey, lemon juice, orange juice, lemon zest, and orange zest to pan. Simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and sauce slightly thickens.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Cook 5 minutes until sauce reduces to desired consistency.
Remove pan from heat. Swirl in cold butter until melted and glossy. Season glaze with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice duck breasts into thick medallions. Arrange duck on plates. Spoon pineapple-ginger glaze over duck. Garnish with toasted almond slivers and fresh thyme or cilantro.
notes: Rendered duck fat can be saved and used for roasting vegetables or potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons is nested in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. A whole, bone-in braised chicken thigh rests centrally on the pasta, showing a rich, caramelized exterior. Small, tender cubes of carrot and celery, along with dark, wrinkled Kalamata olives, are distributed throughout the sauce. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid green garnish. The dish is set on a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Chianti wine
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in wine. Deglaze the pan bottom.
Add tomatoes and olives. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover.
Simmer 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with sauce.
Place pasta in bowls. Top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the wide pasta ribbons
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Sage and Anchovy Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, embodying a simple restaurant style. A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, with its crispy, textured skin, is positioned slightly off-center. The chicken, cooked whole, not sliced, is glistening with the rich, glossy sage and anchovy butter sauce that pools around its base. The sauce exhibits a warm, golden-brown hue, flecked with tiny, dissolved anchovy bits and vibrant green specks of fresh sage. Several whole, crispy fried sage leaves are artfully scattered over and around the chicken, providing a textural contrast and a pop of deep green. A small amount of negative space frames the chicken, enhancing its prominence. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, highlighting the natural colors of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add sage leaves to the pan with residual fat. Fry for 30-60 seconds until crispy. Remove crispy sage. Set aside.
Reduce heat to low. Add anchovy fillets to the pan. Cook, mashing with a spoon, until anchovies dissolve into a paste (about 1-2 minutes).
Add sliced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove pan from heat. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is emulsified and glossy. Do not boil after adding butter.
Taste sauce. Adjust seasoning if needed. Anchovies add salt, so taste before adding more.
Return chicken thighs to the pan with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with crispy sage leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is patted very dry for crispy skin.
Use good quality anchovies; they should dissolve easily and provide umami, not just saltiness.
Do not let the garlic brown, as it can become bitter.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Broccoli Stir-fry is elegantly presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Thin slices of rich, dark brown pan-seared beef are interwoven with vibrant green, crisp-tender broccoli florets. Bright red bell pepper strips and translucent yellow onion slices add contrasting color and texture. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, savory, light brown sauce. The dish is arranged in a balanced, slightly mounded fashion, allowing some negative space on the plate. A sprinkle of diagonally sliced green onions provides a fresh, bright green garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a small, white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed white rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are neatly placed. A folded cotton napkin completes the modern bistro table setting, all illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Use chopsticks for eating, as is traditional in Chinese cuisine.
instructions: Slice beef flank steak thinly against the grain into 0.5 cm strips. Season with salt and pepper.
In a bowl, combine 30 ml soy sauce, 15 ml cornstarch, and 15 ml water. Add beef slices. Toss to coat. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice red bell pepper thinly. Slice yellow onion thinly. Mince garlic. Grate fresh ginger.
Prepare stir-fry sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30 ml soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, remaining 15 ml water or beef broth, and sugar.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add marinated beef. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Remove beef from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add broccoli florets, sliced bell pepper, and sliced onion to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Return cooked beef to the wok with vegetables. Pour stir-fry sauce over ingredients. Toss to coat evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Garnish with diagonally sliced green onions before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Cheese Curd Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Broccoli and Cheese Curd Salad is presented on a rustic ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The plate is generously filled but not overcrowded, showcasing a natural, unpretentious arrangement. Bright green broccoli florets, chopped into bite-sized pieces, form the bulk of the salad. Interspersed throughout are creamy white cheese curds, halved crimson cherry tomatoes, and small, uniform cubes of cooked chicken breast. Finely diced red onion adds flecks of purple. The ingredients are lightly coated in a creamy, off-white dressing, allowing their natural colors and textures to shine. The setting is a cozy, homely kitchen with warm, inviting light. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The overall presentation is comforting and approachable, typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a side dish with grilled meats or sandwiches.
Ideal for potlucks or family gatherings.
instructions: Wash and thoroughly dry broccoli florets. Chop florets into small, bite-sized pieces.
Dice cooked chicken breast into small 1 cm cubes.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Finely dice red onion.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Add chopped broccoli, diced chicken, cheese curds, halved cherry tomatoes, and diced red onion to the bowl with the dressing.
Gently toss all ingredients until evenly coated. Ensure all components are well mixed.
Serve immediately or chill for 30 minutes for flavors to meld.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh, firm broccoli.
Adjust sugar and vinegar in dressing to taste.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F) before dicing.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Chicken and Mushroom Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Garlic Chicken and Mushroom Noodles is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate. Tender egg noodles, lightly coated in savory sauce, form a loose bed. Golden-brown, pan-seared chicken cubes are nestled among them. Earthy, sautéed mushroom slices, deep brown, are scattered throughout, mingling with minced garlic and fresh parsley. A light sheen of sauce coats ingredients. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a standard metal fork and a casually folded cloth napkin nearby. The background features a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen setting under warm, natural light.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add butter to the same pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Meanwhile, cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Return cooked chicken to the pan with the mushroom and garlic sauce. Stir to combine.
Add drained noodles to the pan. Toss gently to coat noodles evenly with the sauce.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir most of the parsley into the noodle mixture. Reserve some for garnish.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Polish-British Braised Pork with Cola-Chocolate Glaze and Zesty Radish-Grapefruit Slaw
recipes.special_requests: Mix of polish and Britain cuisine cuisine, Please use every ingredient! I don't want to waste products
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of deeply braised pork shoulder, cut into large, irregular chunks, rests on a simple, well-used ceramic plate. The rich, dark brown cola-chocolate glaze generously coats the tender pork. Alongside, a vibrant, fresh slaw of finely diced pink grapefruit segments, thinly sliced red radishes, and finely chopped green chili is casually arranged, providing a stark color and texture contrast. A scattering of light, airy, seasoned popcorn is sprinkled over the pork and slaw, adding a unique crunchy element. The plate sits on a rustic wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural light, with a simple fork and knife beside it, evoking a homely, comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rye bread or simple boiled potatoes for dipping into the rich sauce.
A side of sauerkraut could complement the Polish influence.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.quantity: 2, 1 deseeded and sliced for braise, 1 finely chopped for slaw

instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove pork from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in Coca-Cola and chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add bay leaf and chopped dark chocolate. Stir until chocolate melts and sauce is smooth.
Return seared pork to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily pulls apart.

While pork braises, prepare the slaw. In a bowl, combine finely diced grapefruit, thinly sliced radishes, and finely chopped red chili. Squeeze lime juice over the mixture. Season with a pinch of salt. Toss gently. Set aside.
Just before serving, prepare the popcorn. Pop kernels according to package instructions (stove-top or air popper). Season popped corn lightly with salt.
Remove pork from oven. Carefully remove pork chunks from the pot and set aside. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Discard bay leaf.

In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with cold water to create a slurry. Bring the braising liquid to a simmer on the stovetop. Slowly whisk in the cornstarch slurry until the sauce thickens to a desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Return pork chunks to the thickened sauce. Stir to coat.
Serve braised pork and sauce on individual plates. Spoon the zesty grapefruit-radish slaw alongside. Sprinkle a generous amount of seasoned popcorn over the pork and slaw for crunch.
notes: The combination of Coca-Cola and dark chocolate creates a surprisingly rich, complex, and slightly sweet-savory glaze that complements the pork.
The fresh, zesty slaw cuts through the richness of the braised pork, adding brightness and crunch.
The popcorn provides an unexpected, yet delightful, textural contrast.

recipes.recipe_name: Louisiana Shrimp and Smoked Sausage Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A generous, mounded portion of vibrant Louisiana Shrimp and Smoked Sausage Jambalaya fills a deep white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist, infused with a rich reddish-brown hue from the tomato base, and studded with flavorful ingredients. Prominently featured are plump, rosy-orange seared shrimp, cooked to a perfect curl, and thick, dark brown rounds of smoked Andouille sausage. Interspersed throughout are distinct pieces of diced green bell pepper, white onion, and pale green celery, providing color contrast. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley and thin slices of vibrant green scallions garnishes the top, adding freshness. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty French bread.
Offer a bottle of hot sauce for individual preference.
instructions: Slice smoked sausage into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add sliced sausage to the pot. Cook until browned and crisp. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in minced garlic, tomato paste, Cajun seasoning, and dried thyme. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken stock to the pot. Stir well. Bring mixture to a boil.
Add rice and bay leaves. Stir once. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Do not stir.
Remove lid. Stir in browned sausage and shrimp. Gently mix into the rice.
Cover and cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until shrimp turn opaque and pink and rice is tender and has absorbed most liquid.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Remove bay leaves. Fluff Jambalaya with a fork.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley and green onions before serving.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing the 'Holy Trinity' (onion, celery, bell pepper)
Building layers of flavor through browning and deglazing

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Sage and Anchovy Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared cod fillet, featuring a golden-brown crust, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. A glistening, emulsified butter sauce with dissolved anchovy and tender sage leaves pools around the fish. Fresh, vibrant sage leaves and a bright lemon wedge garnish the dish. The plating is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a light wooden table, standard silver flatware, and a white cotton napkin. A small basket of rustic Italian ciabatta bread and a subtle bowl of green olives are in the soft-focused background, enhancing the authentic Italian dining feel. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Pair with a light green salad or simple roasted potatoes.

ingredients.name: Cod fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Carefully place cod fillets into the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F). Remove cod from skillet and set aside on a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 50g butter and 16 whole sage leaves to the skillet. Cook until butter melts and sage leaves crisp slightly, about 2 minutes.
Add anchovy fillets to the skillet. Mash with a spoon until they dissolve into the butter. Add thinly sliced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Let wine reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 3-4 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining 50g cold butter, one piece at a time, whisking constantly to emulsify the sauce. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning if needed. The anchovy provides saltiness.
Return cod fillets to the skillet briefly to coat with sauce. Serve immediately with the sage and anchovy butter sauce spooned over.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Fried Chicken with Cream Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Fried Chicken with Cream Gravy is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Two pieces of golden-brown fried chicken, a drumstick and a thigh, are arranged naturally on the plate. The chicken skin is visibly crispy and textured. A generous pool of creamy, light brown gravy rests beside the chicken, slightly overlapping. The gravy has a smooth, rich consistency. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the chicken and gravy, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen. A simple white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware, a fork and knife, are set to the side. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a comforting atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, showing hints of a lived-in family dining area with subtle, natural clutter, enhancing the home-cooked feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes
Serve with collard greens
Serve with cornbread
instructions: Pat chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels.
In a shallow dish, combine 200 g flour, 15 g salt, 5 g black pepper, 5 g garlic powder, and 5 g paprika. Mix well.
In another shallow dish, whisk eggs and 120 ml milk until combined.
Dredge each chicken piece in the seasoned flour. Shake off excess.
Dip chicken into the egg mixture. Let excess drip off.
Dredge chicken a second time in the seasoned flour, pressing to coat thoroughly. Place on a wire rack.
Heat 750 ml vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat to 175°C.
Carefully add chicken pieces to the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry in batches.
Fry chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.
Remove chicken from oil. Place on a clean wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain excess oil. Season lightly with salt if desired.
To make gravy: Carefully pour off all but 60 ml of the cooking oil from the pot. Place pot over medium heat.
Add 60 g butter to the pot. Melt completely.
Whisk in remaining 50 g flour. Cook, whisking constantly, for 1-2 minutes until a light roux forms.
Gradually whisk in 480 ml milk until smooth. Continue whisking until gravy thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Season gravy with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve fried chicken hot with cream gravy. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety. Use a meat thermometer.
Do not overcrowd the pot when frying chicken to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl contains a vibrant mound of golden-hued short-grain rice. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs rest atop the rice, featuring a deeply seared, crispy bronze skin. Evenly distributed through the rice are 1cm cubes of charred red bell pepper and finely diced translucent onions. The rice is moist and slightly glossy from the olive oil and tomato reduction. Sprigs of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley are scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a rustic light oak table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the crispy skin and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional shallow terracotta dish or paella pan
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Pair with a chilled glass of Spanish Albariño
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion and red pepper in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in grated tomato. Cook for 4 minutes until liquid evaporates.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Grate the tomatoes to remove skins easily while keeping the pulp

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Bean Chili Pot with Cheesy Potato Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Beef & Bean Chili Pot with Cheesy Potato Topping is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The base of the dish is a rich, dark red-brown chili, visible beneath a comforting, slightly uneven layer of creamy, light golden-brown mashed potatoes. Melted, bubbly, golden-orange cheddar cheese forms a delightful crust over the potatoes, with some areas slightly browned. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley or cilantro leaves adds a pop of color and freshness. The ground beef is cooked into the chili base. The bell peppers, carrots, and onions are diced and integrated into the chili. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a homely kitchen setting. A simple, off-white ceramic plate with a subtle rim is placed beneath the bowl. A casually folded beige linen napkin lies beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, mimicking natural kitchen light, creating soft shadows that enhance the comforting appeal of the dish. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment, perhaps with a glimpse of everyday kitchen items. The overall presentation is modest and unpretentious, focusing on hearty, satisfying comfort food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and carrots into 1 cm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Grate the small apple finely.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it up, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, bell peppers, and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and grated apple. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Stir well.
Drain and rinse kidney beans and black beans. Add to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While chili simmers, peel potatoes. Dice into 2 cm cubes.
Place diced potatoes in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pan. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the hot chili mixture into an oven-safe baking dish if not using a Dutch oven.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the chili mixture.
Grate cheddar cheese. Sprinkle generously over the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden brown.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Spinach Curry with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homestyle Chicken and Spinach Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, creamy texture and vibrant colors. Tender chunks of seared chicken are nestled within a thick, emerald-green spinach-infused curry, flecked with darker green spinach pieces. The curry has a natural, slightly glossy sheen. Alongside, a generous scoop of fluffy, white basmati rice sits in a smaller, matching bowl. The dish is casually arranged on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and a traditional Indian steel spoon are placed next to the bowls. Freshly chopped coriander is sprinkled over the curry, adding a bright green contrast. The background hints at a lived-in family kitchen, with minimal, unobtrusive clutter.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt.
Wash basmati rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Use a 1:1.5 rice to water ratio for fluffy rice. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Mince garlic and ginger. Slice green chili thinly.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and green chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in coriander powder, cumin powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides. This takes about 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Pour in chicken stock and coconut cream. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in spinach until wilted. This takes 2-3 minutes.
Add garam masala. Adjust salt to taste. Stir well.
Chop fresh coriander. Stir half into the curry. Reserve half for garnish.
Serve chicken and spinach curry hot with basmati rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Chicken & Beer Broth with Fermented Broccoli & Crispy Skin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, golden chicken and beer broth is presented in a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic bowl. Tender shredded chicken and vibrant green blanched broccoli florets are gently arranged within the liquid, allowing the natural forms to show. A few pale green, crunchy fermented broccoli batons are placed artfully on the surface, alongside irregular pieces of golden, crispy chicken skin, providing textural contrast. The plating is minimalistic, with ample white space around the ingredients. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood table, beside an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its earthy colors and pure textures, set against a clean, uncluttered background.
instructions: Remove chicken skin carefully. Reserve skin. Debone chicken. Place bones, backbone, and wing tips into a large stock pot. Add onion peels, bay leaves, thyme, peppercorns.
Cover bones and aromatics with 2 litres water. Bring to a boil. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 2 hours. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

While broth simmers, cut chicken meat into 2cm chunks. Add chunks to strained broth. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken chunks. Shred or dice. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Lay chicken skin flat on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Season lightly with salt. Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and crispy. Remove. Break into small pieces. Set aside.

Wash and peel broccoli stems. Cut into 5cm batons. In a clean glass jar, dissolve 20g salt in 500 ml filtered water to make a 4% brine. Pack broccoli batons tightly into the jar. Pour brine over broccoli, ensuring stems are fully submerged. Place a fermentation weight or small, clean jar on top to keep stems submerged. Seal loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate when ready.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Return strained chicken broth to heat. Add 250 ml beer. Bring to a simmer. Season broth with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot broth into individual bowls. Add shredded chicken and blanched broccoli florets to each bowl. Garnish with a few pieces of fermented broccoli stem and crispy chicken skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Carrot & Roasted Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Carrot & Roasted Chicken Salad is presented on a handcrafted, light cream ceramic plate, resting on a reclaimed light wood surface. The composition is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing natural textures and colors. A bed of vibrant mixed greens forms the base. Diced roasted chicken chunks are nestled among the greens. Thinly sliced fresh carrot rounds and translucent, slightly lighter fermented carrot rounds are artfully scattered, providing contrasting textures and shades of orange. A light drizzle of garlic vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them visually. Freshly chopped parsley and dill are sprinkled sparingly for a touch of green. The overall impression is one of natural beauty and mindful arrangement. The plate is surrounded by ample negative space, highlighting the individual ingredients. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone and a small, smooth river stone are placed to the side, complementing the eco-conscious theme. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the food's inherent freshness and color.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrots: Wash and thinly slice 300g carrots into rounds. Dissolve 15g non-iodized salt in 500ml filtered water to make brine. Pack carrot slices tightly into a clean glass jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely to allow gas release. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Roast Chicken: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry. Rub with 5ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Place on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into small chunks.
Prepare Salad Components: Wash and dry mixed greens. Peel and thinly slice 100g fresh carrots into rounds.
Make Garlic Vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together 60ml extra virgin olive oil, 30ml apple cider vinegar, 1 minced garlic clove, 5g Dijon mustard, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper until emulsified.

Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, fresh carrot slices, 50g fermented carrot slices, diced roasted chicken, 10g chopped parsley, and 5g chopped dill. Pour vinaigrette over salad. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Black Bean & Tomato Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Fermented Black Bean & Tomato Consommé is presented in a clean, minimalist white ceramic bowl, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The consommé is a clear, amber-hued liquid, shimmering subtly under soft natural light. A few perfectly cooked, dark black beans are scattered sparingly at the bottom of the bowl, visible through the transparent broth. Irregular, reddish-brown shards of crispy tomato skin float delicately on the surface, providing a textural contrast. Small, vibrant green dots of herb stem oil are strategically placed, adding a fresh color accent. The bowl rests on a light, textured bamboo or natural stone surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle hints of natural elements like a simple green plant, maintaining an eco-conscious, minimalistic aesthetic. The composition emphasizes clean lines, natural textures, and the inherent beauty of each ingredient.
instructions: Soak dried black beans overnight. Drain.
Cook soaked beans in fresh water until tender. Drain, reserving all cooking liquid. Set aside 50g cooked whole beans for garnish. Mash 30g fermented black beans into a paste.
Halve tomatoes. Reserve tomato cores, ends, and skins. Roughly chop remaining tomato flesh. Dice half an onion. Smash garlic cloves.
Toss chopped tomato flesh, diced onion, and smashed garlic with a drizzle of olive oil. Roast at 200°C for 15 minutes, until slightly softened.

Combine reserved black bean cooking liquid, roasted tomato cores, ends, skins, onion scraps, carrot scraps, celery scraps, garlic peels, and parsley or cilantro stems in a large pot. Add 2 litres of water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook gently for 45-60 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Return clear broth to a clean pot.
Add mashed fermented black bean paste to the clear broth. Stir well. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.

To make tomato skin crisps: Carefully peel skins from fresh tomatoes (or use some from roasted). Lay flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 120°C until fully dry and crispy. Break into small, irregular shards.
To make herb stem oil: Finely chop remaining parsley or cilantro stems. Blend with 15ml olive oil. Strain through a fine sieve to get clear green oil.
Ladle hot consommé into individual serving bowls. Add a few cooked whole black beans. Garnish with tomato skin crisps and a drizzle of herb stem oil. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste cooking by utilizing vegetable scraps and peels for the broth and garnishes.
The fermentation element adds deep umami and complexity to the consommé.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Cucumber Fermented Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earth-toned, matte finish, showcasing a clean, minimalistic aesthetic. Diced fermented tomatoes, vibrant red, and diced fermented cucumbers, a muted green, are artfully scattered across the plate. Each piece is distinct, allowing natural light to highlight their textures and colors. A light drizzle of the translucent fermented brine dressing glistens over the vegetables. Freshly chopped green dill is sprinkled for a pop of fresh color and natural garnish. Toasted pumpkin seeds are scattered among the vegetables, adding a contrasting texture and earthy tone. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and emphasizing the pure beauty of the ingredients. A blurred, minimalist background with a hint of natural plant life completes the eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Prepare fermentation jar. Ensure it is clean and sterilized.
Combine non-iodized salt and filtered water to create brine. Stir until salt dissolves.
Place diced tomatoes and diced cucumbers into the fermentation jar. Pack them gently.
Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Leave 2-3 cm headspace.
Seal the jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Store at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days. Fermentation is complete when vegetables are slightly tangy.
Once fermented, strain vegetables. Reserve the fermentation liquid.
In a small bowl, whisk together 80ml of the reserved fermentation liquid, extra virgin olive oil, and optional apple cider vinegar. Season with black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine fermented tomatoes and cucumbers with chopped fresh dill.
Pour dressing over vegetables. Toss gently to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Green Pea Mochi
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sweet Green Pea Mochi is presented on a small, simple off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim. Two to three mochi pieces are casually arranged, some touching, others slightly apart. The mochi are roundish, with a naturally soft and slightly irregular shape, lightly dusted with cornstarch. Their exterior is a translucent, soft white, revealing a subtle hint of green from the sweet pea paste filling. The green pea paste, a smooth and dense filling, is fully enclosed within the chewy mochi exterior. The plate sits on a well-used light wooden dining table. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy overhead kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed family dining atmosphere. A small, plain white or light-colored tea cup is visible in the soft background, hinting at a traditional Japanese serving style. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on the comfort and natural appearance of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a warm cup of unsweetened green tea.
Enjoyed as a sweet snack or light dessert after a meal.
instructions: Blend thawed green peas, 60g sugar, 50ml water, and salt until smooth.
Pour pea paste into a small saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until thickened and firm. Set aside to cool completely.
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine glutinous rice flour, 30g sugar, and 200ml water. Whisk until smooth.
Cover bowl loosely with plastic wrap. Microwave on high for 2 minutes.
Stir dough with a wet spatula. Re-cover. Microwave for another 1-2 minutes until dough is translucent and very sticky.
Generously dust a clean work surface with cornstarch.
Scrape hot mochi dough onto the dusted surface.
Dust top of mochi dough with more cornstarch.
Gently flatten dough to about 1 cm thickness using a cornstarch-dusted rolling pin or hands.
Cut dough into 8-10 equal squares or circles.
Place a small spoonful of cooled green pea paste onto the center of each mochi piece.
Gently fold and pinch edges of mochi dough around the paste to seal, forming a ball.
Place finished mochi seam-side down. Lightly dust with more cornstarch before serving.
notes: Best enjoyed fresh on the day of preparation for optimal texture.
Use glutinous rice flour (Mochiko) for the correct chewy mochi texture, not regular rice flour.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Carrot Broth Soup
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain bowl holds a single portion of golden, clear Chicken and Carrot Broth Soup. The translucent broth shimmers, revealing perfectly diced 2 cm chicken breast cubes and vibrant orange 1 cm carrot dice, all submerged but clearly visible. The chicken pieces are tender and uniformly cut. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley floats on the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed neatly beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the clean lines and inviting warmth of the soup, with a subtly blurred bistro-style background creating a casual yet refined atmosphere.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes.
Cut carrots into 1 cm dice or thin rondelles.
Finely dice onion and celery. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and celery. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add diced carrots. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly tender.
Add chicken cubes to the simmering soup. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Shrimp Pasta
