instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Grill or pan-sear chicken until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest for 5 minutes. Cut chicken into bite-sized chunks.
Cook bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain excess fat. Crumble the bacon.
While chicken rests, prepare vegetables. If using large tomatoes, cut into wedges. If using cherry tomatoes, halve them. Drain mozzarella. Wash and dry salad greens.
For the dressing, whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, tomato wedges or halves, and mozzarella. Add chicken chunks and crumbled bacon.
Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.
Tear fresh basil leaves and scatter over the salad just before serving. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Homestyle Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base, topped with hearty, golden-brown chicken chunks. The chicken is seared, showing irregular, appealing edges. Diced orange carrots, vibrant red bell pepper, and translucent yellow onions are scattered generously among the chicken. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish has a natural, unarranged look, as if scooped directly from the skillet onto the plate. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple metal fork resting nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 600ml chicken broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 4-5 minutes until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion, carrots, and bell pepper to the same skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the skillet with vegetables. Stir to combine.
Stir in chopped fresh basil. Serve immediately over cooked rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with earthy tones, resting on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Diced fresh and halved quick-fermented tomatoes, in shades of vibrant red and muted maroon, are artfully scattered amidst crisp 1cm cucumber cubes and creamy chickpeas. Thinly sliced red onion and delicate slivers of red chili provide contrasting accents. A generous drizzle of the chili-lemon dressing coats each ingredient, creating a natural sheen. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is natural and unfussy, celebrating the pure forms and textures of the ingredients. Negative space around the bowl emphasizes the minimalistic aesthetic. A simple, undyed linen napkin and a small, unadorned ceramic spoon complete the eco-conscious table setting. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, vibrant appearance.
instructions: Chop ripe mixed tomatoes into 2cm pieces. Halve quick-fermented cherry tomatoes. Peel and dice English cucumber into 1cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion. Rinse and drain cooked chickpeas. Combine all in a large mixing bowl.

Deseed red finger chili and thinly slice. In a small bowl, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, reserved fermented tomato liquid, and thinly sliced red chili. Season with sea salt and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Add to the salad. Toss again lightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: French Provencal Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French Provencal Chicken and Potato Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain soup bowl. The rich, reddish-orange broth, derived from crushed tomatoes and chicken stock, is clear yet substantial. Tender 2-3cm chunks of cooked chicken and neatly diced 2cm potato cubes are visible, creating a balanced composition. Small pieces of softened tomato are dispersed throughout. The soup is generously garnished with vibrant, finely chopped fresh parsley, adding a pop of green against the warm tones of the soup. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic French flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip and sear other side 3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until liquid reduces by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 45 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot. Let cool slightly. Discard skin and bones. Cut chicken meat into 2-3cm chunks.
Add diced potatoes to the simmering broth. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Return chicken chunks to the soup. Simmer 5 minutes to heat through.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Tortilla with Tomato-Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Spanish Tortilla occupies the center of a clean, white round porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its rustic, hearty appearance. The tortilla is roughly 20-22 cm in diameter and 4-5 cm high, with a slightly irregular, artisanal edge. Its surface is a rich, even golden-brown, indicative of a perfectly cooked egg crust. Peeking from within the firm, custard-like interior are visible chunks of tender, pan-seared chicken, vibrant red slices of chorizo, and soft, lightly browned potato pieces, interspersed with translucent caramelized onion. The textures are varied: firm yet yielding tortilla, tender chicken, slightly crisp chorizo, and soft potato. Beside the tortilla, a small, vibrant mound of fresh tomato-cucumber salad provides a burst of contrasting color and freshness. The salad features 1.5cm diced red tomatoes and green cucumber, with delicate slivers of red onion, glistening lightly with olive oil and vinegar. A single slice of rustic, crusty toasted bread, golden-brown and slightly irregular, rests diagonally against the side of the salad, offering a textural counterpoint. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley over the tortilla. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows that add depth without distracting from the food. Traditional Spanish flatware is placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of olives.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up flavors.
Enjoy with a glass of dry Spanish red wine or a light cerveza.
instructions: Dice chicken into 2cm pieces. Slice chorizo into 1cm rounds, then quarter them.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a 24cm oven-safe, non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add chorizo to the same skillet. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside. Keep rendered fat in the pan.

Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potatoes, cut into 5mm thick slices or small cubes. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly golden, about 15-20 minutes.
Add thinly sliced onion and minced garlic to the skillet with potatoes. Cook until onion softens, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in smoked paprika.
Return chicken and chorizo to the skillet with potatoes and onions. Mix well. Spread ingredients evenly in the pan.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs with milk, salt, and black pepper. Pour egg mixture over ingredients in the skillet. Ensure everything is submerged.
Cook on stovetop over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, until edges are set and bottom is golden.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Transfer skillet to oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until tortilla is set and golden brown on top. Insert a thermometer into the chicken parts to ensure 75°C internal temperature.

While tortilla bakes, prepare salad: Combine 1.5cm diced tomatoes, 1.5cm diced cucumber, and thinly sliced red onion in a bowl. Drizzle with red wine vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.
Let tortilla cool slightly in the skillet before inverting onto a serving plate.
Garnish tortilla with fresh chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature with the tomato-cucumber salad and toasted bread.
notes: The tortilla can be served warm or at room temperature, making it excellent for casual gatherings.
Adjust chorizo quantity based on preferred spiciness and richness.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Bacon and Corn Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rigatoni pasta is loosely piled in the center of a clean, white, round porcelain plate. The rigatoni is coated in a light, glossy, subtly orange-tinted sauce, reflecting the smoked paprika and corn. Visible chunks of golden-brown, crispy diced bacon are scattered throughout the pasta, providing a savory crunch. Bright yellow corn kernels, some lightly caramelized, are interspersed, adding sweetness and visual pop. Fresh, vibrant green arugula leaves are gently folded into the pasta, with some peeking out, providing a contrasting color and peppery freshness. The dish is garnished with a light sprinkle of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese over the top, with a few whole arugula leaves for added visual appeal. The overall composition features warm oranges, yellows, and browns from the pasta, corn, and bacon, beautifully contrasted with the fresh green of the arugula. Textures are varied, including tender pasta, crispy bacon, slightly firm corn, and delicate arugula. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A folded neutral-colored cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, with a clean, minimal background that highlights the food.
instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Leave 15ml bacon fat in the pan. Add olive oil if needed. Add finely diced red onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and corn kernels. Cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until corn is lightly caramelized.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in stock and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add cooked rigatoni to the pan. Toss to coat evenly.
Stir in crispy bacon and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Remove from heat. Fold in arugula leaves. Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Patate
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, rests at the center. Surrounding the chicken are generous chunks of tender, rustic potato wedges, vibrant red and green bell pepper pieces, and earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, all bathed in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. The sauce, thickened naturally, coats the ingredients, showcasing flecks of dried oregano and chopped fresh rosemary. A scattering of bright green fresh parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing the hearty textures and warm, inviting colors of a traditional Italian country dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pane casereccio) to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
A glass of red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese, is a traditional pairing.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red and green bell peppers and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly reduced, about 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, fresh rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Add potato wedges around the chicken.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes if sauce is too thin. Remove bay leaf.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality canned tomatoes.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide more flavor and moisture.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Potatoes with Dill
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Braised Chicken and Potatoes with Dill is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered on a natural light wood table. A bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, golden-brown from searing, rests prominently. Rustic quartered potato chunks and thick-cut carrot batons are nestled around the chicken, coated in a rich, savory braising liquid. The potatoes are tender, holding their shape, contrasting with the tender chicken. A generous sprinkle of vibrant fresh dill sprigs garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and aromatic freshness. The composition is balanced, inviting, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin sits beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish. A small glass bowl of pickled cucumbers and a slice of dark rye bread are subtly placed nearby, honoring Russian traditions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers (solenye ogurtsy).
Offer extra sour cream (smetana) at the table.
Serve with a slice of dark rye bread.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add thick-cut carrot batons and minced garlic. Sauté for another 3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add quartered potato chunks and bay leaf. Ensure potatoes are partially submerged in liquid.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in sour cream until well combined. Stir in half of the chopped fresh dill.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with remaining fresh dill before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to personal preference after braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Onion Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, golden chicken broth is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish, resting on a light reclaimed wood table. The broth is infused with subtle notes from vegetables. Poached chicken meat, cut into irregular, tender chunks, is gently arranged within the broth. Distinct thin slices of translucent fermented onion add a delicate pink hue and textural contrast. A few vibrant green fresh parsley leaves, naturally placed, provide a pop of color. A light drizzle of chive oil, made from discarded chive stems, creates subtle green streaks on the broth's surface. The setting features a simple undyed linen napkin and a minimalist background with soft, natural lighting, emphasizing the dish's purity and sustainable essence.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Onions: Thinly slice 1 large onion. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 10g salt in 250ml water. Pour brine over onions. Ensure onions are submerged. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.

Make Chicken Broth: Pat dry chicken thighs. Season lightly with 5g salt. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown. Flip. Sear other side. Remove chicken from pot.
Add roughly chopped 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 carrot, and 1 celery stalk (or equivalent vegetable scraps) to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add 1.5 litres water and 5g black peppercorns. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. Skim foam as needed.
Remove chicken thighs from broth. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Debone chicken thighs. Shred or dice chicken meat into small chunks. Set aside.
Prepare Chive Oil: Blend chive stems/scraps with 30ml neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to create a clear green oil.

Assemble Soup: Return strained broth to pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add shredded chicken and 60g of fermented onions. Taste broth. Adjust salt if needed. Simmer for 5 minutes to heat through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Ladle soup into bowls. Drizzle lightly with chive oil. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beef and Beer Stew with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Belgian Beef and Beer Stew is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The stew features large, fork-tender beef chunks, rich dark brown from braising, nestled among softened, caramelized onion slices, vibrant red bell pepper chunks, and pieces of diced tomato, all coated in a glossy, thick, dark amber sauce. A generous bed of fluffy, white long-grain rice occupies the base of the bowl. The stew's surface is lightly speckled with freshly chopped bright green parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is robust and comforting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's deep colors and textures, evoking a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette or rye bread for dipping.
Offer a dollop of strong Dijon mustard on the side.
Pair with a glass of the same Belgian dark ale used in the stew.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge beef lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook until softened and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper chunks. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and brown sugar. Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beer, pork stock, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours. Beef should be fork-tender.
While stew cooks, prepare rice. Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs from stew. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve stew immediately over cooked rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use a good quality dark Belgian ale, not a light lager.
Browning the beef thoroughly is crucial for deep flavor development.
The stew can be made a day ahead; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon and Corn Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Creamy Bacon and Corn Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Al dente rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, creamy sauce, with golden-brown crispy bacon pieces (small cubes) and vibrant yellow corn kernels (whole) evenly distributed throughout. A light scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped green parsley adds a fresh contrast on top. The dish has a balanced composition, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. It is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork to the right and a neatly folded white cotton napkin to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors in a professional, approachable restaurant style. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni and cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, dice bacon into 1 cm cubes. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bacon. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the skillet.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Add olive oil to the skillet with bacon fat if needed. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sweet corn kernels to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp.
Pour heavy cream into the skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water. Add drained pasta to the skillet with the cream sauce. Add cooked bacon and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Toss everything together. If the sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Savory Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of One-Pot Savory Chicken and Rice rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a subtle rim, placed on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. Large, rustic chunks of seared chicken thigh, boasting a golden-brown exterior, are nestled among a mound of fluffy, pearly white long-grain rice. The rice is infused with finely diced, translucent sautéed onion and flecks of fresh, chopped green parsley. The dish exudes warmth and comfort, with natural textures and steam gently rising. A standard silver fork is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light, suggesting a relaxed, everyday family meal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with half of the salt and pepper.
Dice the yellow onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot pot. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides, about 4-5 minutes. Do not overcrowd. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Add remaining salt and pepper. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Bring broth to a boil. Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid.
Remove pot from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Stir in fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste after cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Penne
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic pasta bowl. One large, tender chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening with rich tomato sauce, rests prominently atop a generous bed of al dente penne pasta. The vibrant red sauce, infused with diced onions and substantial pieces of red and green bell peppers, coats the pasta and chicken. The sauce has a natural, slightly chunky texture. Fresh, roughly torn green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping in a homely, inviting manner. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a hearty, satisfying portion. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, with a simple cloth napkin casually placed beside the bowl and a traditional fork resting nearby, reflecting a relaxed, family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: small bunch, roughly torn, for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper pieces to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through.
While chicken simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore directly over the cooked pasta. Garnish each portion with fresh torn basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce benefits from a longer, slower simmer, allowing flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fresh Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown crust, is the focal point on a modest, round, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken, presented whole, is nestled in a generous pool of vibrant red tomato-basil sauce. The sauce, made from roughly chopped tomatoes and finely diced onions and garlic, shows a rustic, slightly chunky texture with visible pieces of softened tomato. Fresh, torn dark green basil leaves are stirred into the sauce and also scattered on top of the chicken as a simple garnish. The plating is natural and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The dish is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually folded linen napkin and standard flatware. Warm, inviting natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Serve alongside simple pasta or roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Roughly chop tomatoes. Add chopped tomatoes to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, crushing with a spoon, until they break down into a sauce.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Roughly chop or tear fresh basil leaves. Stir basil into the sauce. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Beer Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is plated in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its creamy, fluid consistency. The plump Arborio rice grains are glistening, coated in a rich, pale golden sauce. Interspersed throughout are tender, golden-brown chicken cubes, approximately 2-3 cm, providing a contrasting texture and color. Finely diced, translucent onion pieces are visible within the creamy rice, along with flecks of bright green, freshly chopped parsley sprinkled generously over the top. A subtle sheen from the melted butter and Parmesan gives the dish an inviting, rich appearance. The overall color palette is warm, with golden-yellows, creamy whites, and hints of green. The plate has appropriate negative space. It is placed on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures. A traditional European-style fork and spoon are neatly placed to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed hot and creamy.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine or a complementary beer.

ingredients.name: Light lager or pale ale beer

instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pot. Add finely diced onion. Cook over medium heat until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice edges are translucent (tostatura).
Pour in beer. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add hot pork stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. Risotto should be fluid, not dry.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and cold butter (mantecatura).
Add seared chicken back to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Check seasoning. Adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately in wide, shallow bowls.
notes: Maintaining constant stirring and adding stock gradually are key to a creamy risotto.
Using hot stock ensures the cooking process is not interrupted, keeping the rice temperature consistent.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Crab Cakes with Peach Salsa
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two golden-brown, pan-seared crab cakes, with a crispy, slightly irregular crust and visible flakes of crab, are centrally placed. Beside them, a small, artfully mounded pile of thinly sliced, sautéed yellow onions and earthy brown cremini mushrooms, cooked until tender and lightly caramelized. A vibrant, fresh peach salsa, featuring small, bright orange peach cubes, finely diced red onion, and flecks of green cilantro, is spooned generously over one side of the crab cakes, creating a dynamic contrast of color and texture. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the individual components. A simple white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its fresh ingredients and inviting textures.

ingredients.name: Finely chopped red onion (for crab cakes)

instructions: Prepare Crab Cakes: In a large bowl, gently combine crab meat, panko, beaten egg, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, red onion, parsley, and Worcestershire sauce (if using).
Season with salt and pepper. Mix gently to avoid breaking crab lumps.
Form mixture into 8 equal patties, about 2.5 cm thick. Place on a plate, cover, and chill for at least 30 minutes. This helps them hold shape.
Prepare Peach Salsa: In a small bowl, combine diced peaches, diced red onion, cilantro, lime juice, salt, and chili flakes (if using). Stir gently. Set aside.
Sauté Mushrooms and Onions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thinly sliced yellow onion. Cook, stirring, until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook until mushrooms release liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in minced garlic during the last minute. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Sear Crab Cakes: Heat neutral oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, carefully place crab cakes in the skillet, ensuring not to overcrowd.
Sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Cook in batches if necessary.

Plate and Serve: Place a portion of sautéed mushrooms and onions on each plate. Arrange two seared crab cakes beside or slightly on top of the vegetables. Spoon a generous amount of peach salsa over or next to the crab cakes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Apple Salad with Crispy Bacon & Crab
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, minimalist salad is presented on a cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The base of cooled white rice provides a neutral canvas. Bright red quick-pickled cherry tomatoes, glossy thin slices of quick-pickled red apple, and vibrant sliced strawberries are artfully arranged across the rice. Scattered among the fresh elements are golden-brown, finely diced crispy bacon and sausage bits, along with delicate flakes of crisped crab meat, adding textural contrast. Toasted, roughly chopped almonds and golden breadcrumbs are sprinkled for crunch. A subtle sheen of dressing coats the ingredients. A fine dusting of dark chocolate is grated over the top. The composition features ample white space, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients under soft, natural lighting. A green plant in the background hints at nature, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled tomatoes: Halve cherry tomatoes. In a small bowl, combine 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 30 ml water, 2 g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add halved tomatoes. Let marinate 15 minutes.

Prepare quick-pickled apples: Thinly slice apple into half-moons. In another small bowl, combine remaining 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 30 ml water, 3 g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add apple slices. Let marinate 15 minutes.

Prepare crispy meats: Finely dice bacon and sausage. Cook bacon and sausage in a dry pan over medium heat until very crispy. Drain on paper towel. Flake crab meat into small pieces. Add flaked crab to the pan with a tiny bit of rendered fat and crisp briefly. Set aside.
Make breadcrumbs: Process stale bread into coarse breadcrumbs. Toast breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Toast almonds: Toast almonds in a dry pan until fragrant. Roughly chop.
Prepare dressing: Mince garlic. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, hot sauce, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.

Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, drained quick-pickled tomatoes, and drained quick-pickled apples. Add sliced strawberries and half of the toasted breadcrumbs and chopped almonds. Drizzle with dressing. Toss gently to combine.

Plate salad: Divide salad among four plates. Arrange components naturally, ensuring colors and textures are visible. Top each serving with crispy bacon, sausage, and crab meat. Garnish with remaining toasted breadcrumbs and chopped almonds. Finely grate dark chocolate over each salad just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Caramelized Onion Salad with Goat Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant salad presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a balanced composition. A bed of fresh, crisp mixed greens forms the base. Warm, deeply caramelized thin slices of yellow onion are artfully scattered over the greens, alongside tender, earthy roasted mushroom slices. The mushrooms are a mix of cremini and shiitake, with a rich brown hue and slightly crispy edges from roasting. Creamy white crumbles of goat cheese are distributed throughout, adding a textural contrast. A glossy balsamic vinaigrette lightly coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. The dish is garnished with a few fresh green thyme leaves. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and standard silver cutlery beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and organized yet organic arrangement, with appropriate negative space around the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Toss sliced mushrooms with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and lightly browned.
In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey. Season the dressing with salt and pepper.
Divide mixed salad greens among four plates.
Arrange warm roasted mushrooms and caramelized onions over the greens.
Crumble goat cheese over each salad.
Drizzle generously with balsamic vinaigrette. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder with Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder is served on a simple, rustic ceramic plate. The pork, cut into irregular, thick chunks, is deeply browned from searing and bathed in a rich, glossy, dark amber pan sauce. Its surface shows tender, pull-apart texture. Alongside, a generous scoop of fluffy, white garlic rice sits, some grains lightly tinted by the sauce. A few strands of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley are scattered casually over the pork and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish is arranged naturally, with components touching and overlapping slightly, creating a comforting, unpretentious feel. The plate is placed on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, showing slight imperfections. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate, and a basic fork rests ready. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Beer
ingredients.quantity: 330 ml (1 bottle/can), dark lager or ale

instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Do in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove pork and set aside.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Cook until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze, releasing browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Add broth. Return seared pork to the pot.
Bring to a simmer. Cover pot. Reduce heat to low.
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shredded with a fork.
While pork braises, prepare garlic rice. Rinse rice.
In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice and 500 ml water. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Cook for 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in 1 minced garlic clove (optional, for fresh garlic flavor in rice).
When pork is done, remove pork chunks from pot. Skim excess fat from sauce if desired.
Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Return pork to sauce or serve pork chunks next to sauce.
Serve pork and sauce over garlic rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Pork shoulder can be replaced with pork belly for a richer dish. Adjust braising time if needed.
The sauce can be strained for a smoother consistency if preferred, but leaving it rustic adds to the home-cooked feel.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Baked Chicken Thighs and Roasted Potatoes sits on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken thigh, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is positioned naturally alongside several irregular, golden-edged roasted potato wedges. Scattered amongst the potatoes are browned lemon slices and tender, roasted garlic cloves. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are casually tucked in, adding a pop of green. The overall arrangement is unpretentious and hearty, reflecting a home-cooked meal. The dish is presented on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, with warm, inviting light casting soft shadows. A simple cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. The scene evokes a comforting, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad
Serve with crusty bread for soaking up juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. No need to peel.
Peel garlic cloves. Leave them whole.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges and whole garlic cloves with 30ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper.
On a large baking tray, arrange seasoned potatoes and garlic in a single layer.
Place seasoned chicken thighs among the potatoes on the baking tray.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Distribute lemon slices over and around the chicken and potatoes.
Tuck rosemary and thyme sprigs among the ingredients.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over everything.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender.
Check chicken internal temperature with a meat thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For crispier chicken skin, ensure chicken is very dry before seasoning.
Do not overcrowd the baking sheet; use two if necessary for even roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Penne and Crusty Bread
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, comforting single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Golden-brown, bone-in chicken pieces, cooked tender, are nestled in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. The sauce is thick with visible chunks of diced red and green bell peppers and soft, sweet diced onions. A generous portion of al dente penne pasta, lightly coated in the same savory sauce, is arranged alongside the chicken. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are torn and scattered over the dish as a simple garnish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A torn piece of crusty ciabatta bread rests casually beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy light, evoking a homely family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of red wine
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and dried basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
While chicken simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Serve chicken and sauce over cooked penne. Garnish with fresh basil.
Serve with crusty bread on the side.
notes: For best flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces.
Leftovers are excellent the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Kali Mirch with Coconut Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a light wooden table. Fluffy white basmati rice forms a neat mound. Beside it, generous chunks of golden-brown chicken, seared and simmered, are bathed in a rich, vibrant yellow-orange curry sauce. The sauce, thick and aromatic, is infused with diced tomatoes, minced garlic, grated ginger, and wilted spinach leaves. Fresh green coriander leaves are scattered over the curry, and a lime wedge rests nearby. The chicken pieces are approximately 3-4 cm chunks. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing the sauce to pool appealingly. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, with a subtle, blurred modern bistro background. A white cotton napkin and traditional Indian flatware complete the individual portion setting. A small ceramic bowl of Indian pickles is subtly visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or roti
Offer a side of raita (yogurt dip) or pickled vegetables (achar)
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Rinse basmati rice. Combine rice with 500ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Heat coconut oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until aromatic.
Add seasoned chicken chunks to the pan. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in diced tomato, chicken stock, and coconut milk. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 10-12 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and chicken to become tender.
Stir in Greek yogurt and fresh spinach. Cook for 2-3 minutes until spinach wilts.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh chopped coriander and squeeze in lime juice. Serve hot with basmati rice.
traditional_techniques: Bhunao (sautéing aromatics and spices to develop deep flavor)

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Red Wine Chicken and Tuna Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic stew fills a deep, earthy ceramic bowl, centered on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table. The stew features robust, browned chicken chunks and soft, diced potatoes. Vibrant green broccoli florets are scattered throughout. The rich, dark red wine-infused broth coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of flaked tuna and finely minced red jalapeno adding texture and color. The broth is thick and hearty, naturally flowing within the bowl. A simple metal spoon rests casually in the bowl. The background shows a casually draped linen napkin and hints of a lived-in kitchen, bathed in soft, natural light, emphasizing a comforting home-cooked meal.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, skinless, cut into 3 cm cubes
Potatoes, peeled, cut into 2 cm cubes
Canned tuna in oil, drained, flaked

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Season chicken cubes with salt and pepper. Add chicken to pot. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken.
Add chopped onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced jalapeño. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pot. Simmer 3 minutes, reduce slightly.
Return chicken to pot. Add diced potatoes, chicken broth, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Add broccoli florets. Cook 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Stir in flaked tuna. Heat through 2 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust jalapeño quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef & Mushroom Macaroni & Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A deep, pristine white porcelain bowl holds a vibrant, hearty meal. A generous base of fluffy white rice supports a rich, savory mixture of well-browned ground beef and earthy, sautéed mushroom slices, all coated in a light, cheesy sauce with al dente macaroni. Around the edges of the central mound, bright green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are arranged. A bold drizzle of vibrant red hot sauce zigzags across the beef and macaroni, adding a pop of color. Scattered over the top are golden, irregularly shaped tortilla crisps, providing a textural contrast. A small sprig of fresh oregano or parsley sits atop the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the bowl, and natural, even lighting that highlights the food's textures and colors. Standard silver flatware is placed beside the bowl.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cook macaroni in boiling salted water until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Brown beef, breaking it apart. Drain any excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and liquid has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef broth. Bring mixture to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Stir cooked macaroni into the beef mixture. Add grated cheddar cheese. Mix until cheese is melted and creamy.
Steam or lightly roast broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Do not overcook.
Cut tortillas into strips or triangles. Toss with a small amount of olive oil. Bake or pan-fry until crisp and golden brown. Season with a pinch of salt.
To assemble, place cooked rice in the bottom of each deep serving bowl. Spoon the beef and macaroni mixture generously over the rice.
Arrange steamed broccoli florets around the edge of the beef and macaroni. Drizzle hot sauce over the dish as desired.
Garnish with the crispy tortilla pieces and a small sprig of fresh oregano or parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Potatoes and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently at the center, its skin crisp and glistening. Surrounding the chicken are tender, rustic 2-3 cm potato chunks and soft, diced onions, all generously coated in a rich, deep reddish-orange braising sauce infused with smoked paprika and saffron. The sauce has a glossy, appealing sheen, pooling slightly around the ingredients. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a vibrant contrast and freshness. The dish is arranged organically, showcasing the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze, loosening any browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce.
Add potato chunks around the chicken. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 30-40 minutes. Cook until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Chicken with Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared boneless chicken thighs, golden-brown, are presented as whole pieces on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside the chicken, a neat scoop of fluffy white rice, lightly studded with vibrant green chopped parsley, is positioned. The chicken is generously draped with a creamy, pale yellow mustard sauce, glistening subtly. A few finely diced caramelized onions are visible within the sauce, adding texture. The plate offers moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with elegant, unadorned flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting colors and textures, set against a blurred, casual bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a classic accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add finely diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Whisk in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

While chicken cooks, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice with 400 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Remove chicken from heat. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish chicken and sauce with remaining fresh parsley before serving.
notes: For extra flavor, consider adding a splash of dry white wine (e.g., Sauvignon Blanc) after sautéing the onions and garlic, before adding the broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Tomato and Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist, natural aesthetic on a handcrafted, undyed ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. A mound of fluffy, light brown herbed rice forms the base, its natural texture visible, flecked with finely chopped green parsley and thyme. Beside the rice, a single, golden-skinned slow-cooked chicken thigh sits, its skin rendered crisp and deeply caramelized, contrasting with the tender, moist meat underneath. Scattered around the chicken and rice are a few whole, plump, lacto-fermented cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled and their colors ranging from deep red to lighter orange-red, offering a subtle visual pop and a hint of tang. A delicate drizzle of the chicken's natural braising liquid glistens subtly. The presentation is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. A few small, fresh green herb leaves are artfully placed for a subtle, natural garnish. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, with soft, natural lighting illuminating the scene. The background is simple and clean, perhaps with a blurred hint of natural greenery or an organic element, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. A single individual portion is shown, highlighting the pure beauty of each ingredient. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced.

ingredients.name: Ripe cherry tomatoes or small roma tomatoes
Fresh rosemary or thyme sprig (for fermentation)
Short-grain brown rice or basmati rice

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes (minimum 5-7 days in advance):
Wash tomatoes. Pierce each tomato once with a clean skewer.
Place tomatoes and herb sprig in a clean jar.
Dissolve 8g salt in 400ml filtered water to make brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 5-10 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.
Prepare Chicken:
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 2-3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Add 100ml water or broth to the pot. Cover tightly.
Braise chicken for 30-40 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot. Rest for 5 minutes. Reserve braising liquid.
Cook Herbed Rice:
Rinse rice thoroughly until water runs clear.
In a medium saucepan, heat 5ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add rinsed rice. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in 600ml vegetable broth or water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley and thyme leaves. Fluff with a fork.
Assemble Dish:
Spoon a generous portion of herbed rice onto each plate.
Place one slow-cooked chicken thigh beside the rice.
Arrange a few fermented tomatoes around the chicken and rice.
Drizzle a small amount of the reserved chicken braising liquid over the chicken and rice.
Garnish with a few small fresh herb leaves.
Finish with a minimal drizzle of good quality olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Shepherd's Pie is presented in a pristine white oval gratin dish, centrally placed on a dark wooden table. The golden-brown mashed potato topping, with delicate fork ridges, forms a rustic crust. Peeking from beneath the potato, the rich, savory lamb mincemeat filling reveals a deep, earthy brown color with flecks of green herbs and diced vegetables. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the potato. Beside the gratin dish, a slice of perfectly toasted, crusty bread rests on the table. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple cotton napkin is folded neatly to the left, and a classic silver fork and knife are positioned to the right. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and warm tones against a subtly blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with green vegetables like peas or green beans.
A dollop of HP Sauce or ketchup is a common accompaniment in British homes.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into equal chunks. Place in a large pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender (about 15-20 minutes). Drain well.
Return drained potatoes to the hot pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry. Mash thoroughly. Add milk, 30g butter, salt, and pepper. Mash until smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add lamb mincemeat. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in red wine and deglaze the pan. Let it simmer until reduced by half.
Add beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, chopped thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Spoon the mincemeat filling evenly into individual oven-safe gratin dishes or a single large oven-safe dish. Spread the mashed potato evenly over the mincemeat, using a fork to create ridges on top. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese if desired.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
While pie bakes, toast or grill the bread slices until golden.
Let the pies rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with toasted bread on the side.
notes: For a thicker sauce, stir in 15g of flour with the tomato paste before adding liquids.
Ensure potatoes are very dry before mashing for a smooth, lump-free texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Creamy Macaroni Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate. A generous, rounded mound of golden-brown macaroni gratin occupies the center, its surface visibly bubbly with a crisp, toasted crust. Resting against the gratin are two to three thick medallions of pan-seared duck breast. The duck skin is visibly crispy and deeply golden-brown, contrasting with the tender, medium-rare pink interior. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley adorns both the duck and the gratin, adding a fresh color pop. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and rich colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant aesthetic against a softly blurred bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in a cold, oven-safe pan. Cook over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes. Render fat until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip duck breasts. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare.
Remove duck from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes. Reserve rendered duck fat.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
While pasta cooks, prepare cheese sauce. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced shallots. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes until thickened.
Whisk in heavy cream and chicken stock. Simmer 3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Gruyere and Parmesan cheeses until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Remove thyme leaves from sprigs. Stir in thyme leaves.
Combine drained macaroni with cheese sauce. Pour into an oven-safe gratin dish (approx. 20x20 cm or similar).
Bake gratin for 15-20 minutes. Top should be golden and bubbly.
Slice rested duck breasts into thick medallions.
Serve macaroni gratin warm. Top each portion with duck medallions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Duck fat can be saved for future cooking.
Ensure duck is rested properly for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Corn Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Corn Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic bowl, reflecting minimalistic elegance. Fluffy, earthy brown rice forms the base, its natural texture prominent. Golden-brown, seared 2cm chicken cubes are neatly arranged atop, their edges subtly crisp. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant pile of pale yellow fermented corn kernels adds contrasting texture and color. Delicate, translucent slices of bright pink pickled red onion are artfully placed, offering visual tang. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green dill provides a natural final touch. The composition is clean and uncrowded, allowing each ingredient to stand out. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded, undyed natural linen napkin. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, emphasizing ingredients' colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background with subtle green foliage.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Corn: Combine 200g corn kernels with 250ml water, 5g salt, 2 crushed garlic cloves, and 2.5g peppercorns in a clean jar. Seal. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until bubbly and slightly sour. Refrigerate.

Prepare Pickled Red Onion: Thinly slice half a red onion. In a small pot, combine 125ml white vinegar, 125ml water, 15g sugar, 5g salt, and 2.5g peppercorns. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over sliced onion in a heatproof jar. Cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Cook Rice: Rinse 300g brown rice. In a pot, combine rice with 750ml chicken stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Cook Chicken: Dice 600g chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Sear for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Sauté Aromatics: Dice remaining half red onion and 2 garlic cloves. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a pan. Add diced onion and garlic. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened.
Combine: Gently fold sautéed aromatics into the cooked brown rice.
Assemble Bowls: Divide rice mixture among 4 bowls. Top each with seared chicken cubes, a spoonful of fermented corn, and a few pickled red onion slices. Garnish with fresh dill or parsley.
notes: Use chicken bones (if using bone-in chicken) and vegetable scraps (onion peels, garlic ends, corn cobs) to make a simple homemade stock for the rice. This maximizes resource use.
Compost any remaining organic waste.
Store leftover fermented and pickled items in the refrigerator for future use.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Caramelized Shrimp Coconut Sticky Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dessert plate, reflecting a modern bistro style. A mound of glossy, creamy white coconut sticky rice forms the base, its soft texture visible. Nestled beside or atop the rice are small, irregular chunks of crispy caramelized shrimp. The shrimp pieces exhibit a deep, rich amber hue from the caramelization, with a slight sheen, suggesting a delicate crispness. Interspersed among the shrimp are flecks of bright red chili, if used, adding a subtle color contrast. A sprinkle of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes is scattered over the dish, providing textural interest. Fine strands of bright green lime zest are artfully placed, offering a pop of fresh color and fragrance. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, emphasizing the dish's unique flavors and textures. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, designed to highlight the unusual yet harmonious blend of sweet, savory, and aromatic elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a small, elegant dessert spoon. The dish embodies the Southeast Asian culinary tradition of balancing sweet and savory flavors, often featuring glutinous rice and coconut milk as staples.
instructions: Rinse glutinous rice several times until water runs clear. Soak rice in cold water for at least 4 hours, or overnight. Drain well.
Steam rice in a steamer basket lined with cheesecloth for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and translucent.
While rice steams, combine 250 ml coconut milk, 50 g palm sugar, and 2 g salt in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Do not boil. Keep warm.
Transfer steamed rice to a bowl. Pour warm coconut syrup over rice. Stir gently to combine. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes to allow rice to absorb the liquid.
Pat shrimp very dry with paper towels. Dice shrimp into 0.5 cm small cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add diced shrimp. Stir-fry quickly until shrimp turns pink and is just cooked through, about 2-3 minutes. Remove shrimp from pan.
In the same pan, add 50 g palm sugar and 30 ml water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves and mixture bubbles. Cook without stirring until caramel turns amber.

Reduce heat to low. Add cooked shrimp, fish sauce, and minced chili to the caramel. Stir quickly to coat shrimp evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until shrimp is well-glazed and slightly crispy. Remove from heat immediately. Spread shrimp on a plate to cool slightly and prevent sticking.

For each serving, place a mound of warm coconut sticky rice on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. Arrange a spoonful of crispy caramelized shrimp on top or beside the rice. Garnish with toasted coconut flakes and fresh lime zest. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Tofu and Broccoli Stir-fry with Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Tofu and Broccoli Stir-fry is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous mound of fluffy, bright white garlic rice sits on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the rice, golden-brown, crispy pan-fried tofu cubes are artfully arranged alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. Thinly sliced, translucent onion pieces are interspersed throughout the stir-fry. A glossy, rich brown savory sauce lightly coats the tofu and broccoli, creating an appealing sheen. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds and finely chopped bright green onion batons, adding contrasting color and texture. The overall composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, highlighting the fresh ingredients and professional cooking. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a set of dark wooden chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting with an authentic East Asian culinary touch. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting colors and textures.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into 2 cm large cubes.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice onion thinly. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Combine soy sauce, vegetable broth, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, and half of the minced garlic in a small bowl. Whisk well.
In a separate small bowl, mix cornstarch with water to create a slurry.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add sliced onion and remaining minced garlic. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add broccoli florets. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Pour the sauce mixture into the wok. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Return crispy tofu to the wok. Toss gently to coat with the sauce.
Serve immediately over garlic rice. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Potato, and Tuna Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken, Potato, and Tuna Bake sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The portion is naturally scooped, revealing a golden-brown, crisped cheddar top. Beneath, tender, pale yellow potato rounds are layered with creamy white sauce, shredded chicken, and flaky tuna. Bright green parsley flecks add a fresh accent. The color palette is warm, inviting, with golden, creamy, and soft yellow tones. The texture appears comforting. The plate rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, with a casual beige napkin and silver fork. Warm, diffused lighting creates a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, ensuring a homely, unpretentious presentation focused on comforting food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Bake chicken thighs for 20-25 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let cool slightly. Shred chicken into bite-sized pieces.
While chicken bakes, slice potatoes into 3mm thick rounds.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Then gradually whisk in heavy cream.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring, until thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Layer half of the potato slices evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Spread shredded chicken over potatoes.
Flake drained tuna evenly over chicken.
Pour half of the cream sauce over the layers.
Top with remaining potato slices. Pour remaining sauce over potatoes.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of One-Pot Chicken and Rice is presented on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Tender, whole chicken thigh pieces are nestled on a bed of fluffy long-grain rice. The rice is naturally mounded, mixed with visible bright green whole peas and vibrant orange sliced carrot rounds. The chicken is golden brown from searing, showing a rustic texture. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color to the top. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, cozy light, typical of a family kitchen. The overall presentation is casual and inviting, reflecting comforting home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with half the salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced carrots. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in rice, dried thyme, remaining salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken is cooked through to 75°C.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and rice onto plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Skillet on a simple, round ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Large, irregular chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled among quartered, tender potatoes and softened, rustic-cut pieces of red bell pepper, sautéed mushrooms, and caramelized onion. A light, savory pan sauce coats the ingredients. The colors are natural and inviting: warm browns from the chicken and mushrooms, vibrant red from the bell pepper, and creamy white from the potatoes. A few fresh green basil leaves are scattered on top for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is casual and natural, typical of a home-cooked meal, with components slightly overlapping.
