Stir in rinsed cannellini beans. Cover and let rest off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not stir the rice too much after adding the broth to allow for proper absorption and avoid stickiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Beef and Potato Roast with Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Skillet Beef and Potato Roast is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, seared beef cubes, approximately 2.5 cm, are nestled among golden-brown roasted potato cubes, 2 cm in size. Vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, about 1.5 cm, intermingle with soft, caramelized thin onion slices. A generous layer of melted, bubbly sharp cheddar cheese, golden-orange in hue, drapes over the ingredients, creating a rich, inviting appearance. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is organized yet natural, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and warm colors in a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add beef in a single layer. Sear until browned on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Remove beef from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened and lightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
Add bell pepper strips and minced garlic. Cook for 3-4 minutes until peppers slightly tender.
Stir in potato cubes, diced tomatoes (undrained), beef broth, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Cover skillet. Transfer to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Cook for 25 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir gently. Arrange ingredients evenly.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over the top.
Return to oven. Cook uncovered until cheese is melted and bubbly, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove from oven. Discard thyme and rosemary sprigs.
Let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Plant-Based Beef Medallions with Black Olive & Raspberry Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Seared Plant-Based Beef Medallions with Black Olive & Raspberry Risotto is presented on an elegant, matte white bone china plate with a subtle, organic texture. The creamy, fluid risotto forms an artistic, flowing pool on one side of the plate, its pale, earthy hue subtly flecked with dark, finely chopped Kalamata olives and vibrant crimson bursts from whole fresh raspberries. A perfectly seared, dark brown plant-based beef medallion, retaining its robust shape, rests precisely beside the risotto. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the deliberate placement of each component. A few additional fresh raspberries and a delicate sprig of fresh thyme are meticulously placed as precise garnishes. The setting features a premium white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows to enhance depth and texture. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole, captivating focal point.
instructions: Heat 15ml olive oil and half the vegan butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of rice grains become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Heat vegetable broth in a separate saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.

Add one ladleful of hot broth to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is almost fully absorbed. Continue adding broth ladle by ladle, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
After 15 minutes, stir in the finely chopped Kalamata olives.

Continue adding broth. When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, remove from heat. Stir in remaining vegan butter and half of the fresh raspberries. Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid and free-flowing.
While risotto cooks, heat a separate heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add a generous drizzle of olive oil.

Season plant-based beef medallions with salt and pepper. Place medallions in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and heated through. Adjust cooking time based on product instructions.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of the fluid risotto onto the center of each plate, creating an organic, flowing shape. Do not form a ring.
Carefully place one seared plant-based beef medallion alongside the risotto. Do not slice or fan.
Artistically scatter a few remaining fresh raspberries and a sprig of fresh thyme on the plate. Garnish with a small cluster of microgreens.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Crab & Tuna Cakes with Potato-Onion Puree and Cocoa Nage
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, featuring a harmonious balance of colors and textures. At the plate's center, a smooth, pale cream-colored mound of potato-onion puree is elegantly placed, its surface gently mounded. Beside it, two golden-brown, pan-seared crab and tuna cakes are positioned, showcasing their lightly crisp, textured exterior. The cakes are thick, retaining their natural shape. A rich, glossy, dark brown cocoa nage is subtly spooned around the base of the puree and cakes, creating a delicate pool. Bright green snipped chives are scattered over the cakes and puree, providing a fresh, vibrant contrast. The composition is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and standard flatware under natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: canned crab meat, drained and flaked
canned tuna in oil, drained and flaked
potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Prepare Potato-Onion Puree: Boil potato chunks in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Separately, sauté roughly chopped onion in a small amount of olive oil until very soft and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Drain potatoes well. Combine cooked potatoes and sautéed onion in a pot. Add milk, butter, salt, and pepper. Mash or blend until smooth. Keep warm.

Prepare Crab & Tuna Cakes: In a large bowl, combine flaked crab meat, flaked tuna, finely diced onion, breadcrumbs, beaten egg, mayonnaise, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix. Form into 8 equal patties, about 2 cm thick.

Cook Crab & Tuna Cakes: Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Carefully place patties in the hot oil. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan.

Prepare Cocoa Nage: In a small saucepan, heat 5 ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add minced shallot and cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat. Add chopped dark chocolate. Whisk until chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of warm potato-onion puree onto the center of each plate. Arrange two seared crab and tuna cakes beside the puree. Gently spoon a small amount of cocoa nage around the base of the puree and cakes. Garnish with snipped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure crab and tuna are well-drained to prevent soggy cakes.
Do not overmix the cake mixture to maintain a flaky texture.
The cocoa nage is subtle; it adds richness and depth, not sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Comte and Spinach Soufflé with Quick-Pickled Artichoke
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, french fusion, healthy, high protein, low carb
recipes.visual_description: A golden-crusted, dramatically risen soufflé stands proudly in a white, round ceramic ramekin, centered on a light bamboo or stone table. Its top is a rich, warm golden brown, lightly crinkled, indicating a perfectly cooked exterior. Beside it, a small, artfully arranged pile of diced quick-pickled artichoke hearts gleams with a soft, pale yellow hue, punctuated by toasted pine nuts. Finely chopped vibrant green chives are scattered over the artichoke and pine nuts, adding fresh contrast. The overall presentation is minimalistic and clean, with ample negative space. The handcrafted ceramic plate is a natural cream or beige. Soft, diffused natural light highlights textures and colors. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly in the background.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Artichoke: In a small pot, combine white wine vinegar, water, erythritol, salt, and thyme. Bring to a simmer. Add diced artichoke hearts. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool completely in liquid.
Preheat Oven: Preheat oven to 190°C. Butter and lightly dust a 250 ml soufflé ramekin with grated Comte.
Prepare Soufflé Base: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain well. Squeeze out all excess water. Chop spinach finely.

Make Roux: In a small saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add almond flour. Stir for 1 minute until a paste forms. Gradually whisk in almond milk until smooth and slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Finish Soufflé Base: Stir in grated Comte, chopped spinach, nutmeg, salt, and pepper into the milk mixture. Stir until Comte melts. Whisk in egg yolks, one at a time, until well combined.
Whip Egg Whites: In a clean, dry bowl, whip egg whites with a pinch of cream of tartar (if using) until stiff peaks form.

Combine Soufflé: Gently fold one-third of the egg whites into the spinach-Comte mixture to lighten it. Then, carefully fold in the remaining egg whites until just combined, being careful not to deflate the mixture.
Bake Soufflé: Pour mixture into the prepared ramekin. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until puffed, golden brown, and set. Do not open oven door during baking.
Toast Pine Nuts: While soufflé bakes, toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium-low heat until golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Serve: Carefully remove soufflé from oven. Serve immediately in its ramekin. Spoon some quick-pickled artichoke and toasted pine nuts alongside or on top. Garnish with fresh chives.
notes: This recipe emphasizes eco-conscious cooking by utilizing quick-pickling for preservation and focusing on a single, zero-waste portion.
The plant-forward approach highlights eggs, spinach, artichoke, and pine nuts as main protein and nutrient sources.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken, Bacon & Shrimp Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, hearty portion of Spicy Chicken, Bacon & Shrimp Pasta is presented in a well-used ceramic bowl, resting on a rustic wooden kitchen table. The pasta, likely penne or rigatoni, is coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce. Visible are tender, irregular chunks of seared chicken, plump pink shrimp, and crispy, golden-brown diced bacon. Halved dark olives are interspersed throughout, adding a visual contrast. The dish is topped with a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, providing a pop of color. The overall plating is natural and unpretentious, with components casually overlapping. Colors are warm and inviting, reflecting the cooked ingredients. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen light, highlighting the textures of the al dente pasta, the firm shrimp, and the crispy bacon. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed beside the bowl, creating a lived-in, homely family dining atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the modest, home-style portion.

ingredients.name: Fresh red chili, minced (or 1 tsp chili flakes)

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserve 125ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken and shrimp with salt and pepper.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave bacon fat in the pan.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the pan if needed. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, hot sauce, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and halved olives to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes until shrimp are pink and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C for chicken).
Add cooked pasta, crispy bacon, and lemon juice to the pan. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water if sauce is too thick.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Quinoa-Walnut Cakes with Fermented Cucumber Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Quinoa-Walnut Cakes is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-beige ceramic plate, on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Two perfectly round, golden-brown quinoa-walnut cakes, approximately 7 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are placed slightly off-center. Their surfaces are textured, showing a crisp, seared finish. Adjacent, a vibrant mound of fermented cucumber slaw features thin, translucent half-moon slices of cucumber intermingled with bright green blanched edamame. A delicate, creamy white coconut-lime-chili emulsion is artfully drizzled over the cakes and onto the plate, creating natural, flowing lines. Ample negative space surrounds the dish. Fresh green coriander leaves and a thin lime curl serve as natural garnishes. The minimalist setting includes an undyed linen napkin and soft, diffused natural lighting, with a clean background hinting at subtle green plants.
instructions: Rinse quinoa. Cook quinoa with 400 ml water and a pinch of salt until fluffy. Set aside to cool.
Prepare flax egg: Combine flaxseed meal and 60 ml water. Let sit 5 minutes until thickened.

Finely chop 10 g ginger, half chili, and garlic. Roughly chop 100 g walnuts. Combine with cooked quinoa, flax egg, 15 g chopped coriander, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix well. Form into 8 equal cakes, approximately 2 cm thick.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook quinoa-walnut cakes 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp. Keep warm.

Prepare fermented cucumber slaw: Thinly slice cucumber into half-moons. In a bowl, combine cucumber with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Let sit 15 minutes. Drain excess liquid. Add shelled edamame and remaining 15 g chopped coriander.

Make coconut-lime-chili emulsion: Finely mince remaining 10 g ginger and other half chili. Zest one lime. Juice both limes. In a blender, combine coconut milk, minced ginger, minced chili, lime juice, and lime zest. Blend until smooth. Season with salt to taste.

To serve, place two quinoa-walnut cakes on each plate. Arrange a mound of fermented cucumber slaw next to the cakes. Drizzle generously with coconut-lime-chili emulsion. Garnish with a few fresh coriander leaves and a thin lime curl.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing full ingredients, such as lime zest, and promoting seasonal, plant-forward eating.
The quick fermentation of cucumber enhances flavor and adds probiotic benefits.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Apple Pasta with Chicken
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, a generous individual portion of Roasted Tomato and Apple Pasta with Chicken forms a balanced mound. Al dente pasta, possibly fusilli or penne, is coated in a light, glossy sauce. Interspersed are vibrant red roasted cherry tomato halves, some slightly collapsed, alongside golden-brown, lightly sautéed apple cubes. Tender, irregularly shaped chunks of seared chicken breast, cooked to 75°C, are visibly integrated, showcasing their golden crusts. Bright green torn basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing fresh contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The dish exhibits natural, complementary colors and varied textures. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures. The background is a soft blur of a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Toss tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, half minced garlic, salt, pepper. Spread on baking tray.
Roast tomatoes for 20 minutes until softened and slightly browned.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Core and cut apples into 1.5 cm cubes.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add remaining minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add apple cubes to pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until slightly tender and lightly caramelized.
Deglaze pan with balsamic vinegar. Scrape up any browned bits.
Add roasted tomatoes, cooked chicken, and chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained pasta to the pan. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir into pasta mixture.
Adjust seasoning if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty chicken and vegetable soup is presented in a clean, off-white ceramic bowl. The soup features clearly visible, evenly diced pieces of tender white chicken breast, bright orange carrot cubes, soft, pale yellow potato chunks, and vibrant red tomato pieces. These ingredients are suspended in a rich, reddish-orange broth, indicating a savory, tomato-infused base. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley or oregano garnishes the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures appear inviting and comforting. The bowl is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin and a plain metal spoon rest beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam rising gently from the hot soup. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary bistro setting without distraction, keeping the focus entirely on the appealing dish.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice carrots into 1 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Dice fresh tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces.
Melt butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in tomato paste, diced fresh tomatoes, diced potatoes, dried oregano, and black pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Season the soup with salt to taste.
Ladle the hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or oregano if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Huevos Rancheros with Crispy Bacon and Spiced Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Huevos Rancheros is elegantly presented on a rustic white ceramic plate. Two lightly crisped corn tortillas form the foundation, each generously covered with a rich, chunky red ranchera sauce. Nestled atop the sauce are two perfectly fried sunny-side-up eggs, their bright yellow yolks glistening. Beside the tortillas, a substantial mound of golden-brown roasted potato cubes, seasoned with chili and cumin, offers a textural contrast. Crispy, thick-cut bacon chunks are scattered artfully over the potatoes and alongside the eggs, adding a savory crunch. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprinkle of bright green chopped cilantro and thin rounds of red serrano pepper for a subtle kick. A vibrant green lime wedge sits invitingly on the plate's edge, ready for a squeeze. The presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer additional salsa or hot sauce on the side.
Accompany with black beans or refried beans.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml vegetable oil, 2.5 g cumin, 2.5 g paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon, drain on paper towels. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in the skillet. Once cooled, chop bacon into chunks.

For the ranchera sauce, dice half the onion and mince garlic. Mince jalapeño/serrano (remove seeds for less heat). Dice tomatoes. Heat reserved bacon fat in the skillet. Sauté diced onion, garlic, and jalapeño/serrano 3-4 minutes until softened.

Add diced tomatoes, remaining 2.5 g cumin, and 2.5 g paprika to the skillet. Simmer 10-12 minutes, crushing tomatoes with a spoon, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Partially mash or blend for a chunkier sauce.
Warm corn tortillas. You can lightly fry each tortilla in a dry hot skillet 15-20 seconds per side, or warm in microwave/oven until pliable.
Fry eggs in a separate skillet with 15 ml fresh vegetable oil over medium heat. Cook sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks are runny.

To assemble each serving: Place two warm tortillas on a plate. Spoon generous amounts of ranchera sauce over each tortilla. Carefully place one fried egg on top of each sauced tortilla. Arrange roasted potato cubes next to the tortillas. Scatter chopped crispy bacon chunks over the potatoes and around the eggs. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and thin slices of serrano pepper. Serve with a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi with Sage Butter and Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of golden potato gnocchi is artfully arranged on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gnocchi are plump and irregularly shaped, with visible ridges, some exhibiting a light golden-brown sear from pan-tossing, showcasing their tender texture. Interspersed among the gnocchi are vibrant red roasted cherry tomatoes, some whole and glistening, others gently burst, releasing their sweet juices. Fresh, crisp sage leaves, some lightly fried to a darker green, are scattered throughout, adding color and aromatic contrast. A delicate sheen of golden-brown butter coats the dish. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a creamy, savory finish. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the remaining sauce.
Pair with a glass of light red wine like Chianti or a crisp white like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pierce potatoes with a fork. Roast whole potatoes for 60-75 minutes, or until very tender.
Halve roasted potatoes. Scoop flesh into a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Do not overwork. Spread hot mashed potato on a clean surface to cool slightly for 5 minutes.
Form a well in the center of the potato. Add flour, egg yolk, and 5g salt. Gently bring ingredients together. Knead briefly until just combined into a soft, cohesive dough. Do not over-knead.

Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion into a 2 cm thick rope. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Gently roll each piece over a gnocchi board or fork tines for ridges. Place shaped gnocchi on a floured baking sheet.
While making gnocchi, toss cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, sliced garlic, 3g salt, and 2g black pepper on a baking tray. Roast at 200°C for 15-20 minutes, until softened and slightly burst.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
In a large skillet, melt 100g butter over medium heat. Add sage leaves. Cook until butter is golden brown and sage is crispy, about 3-5 minutes. Be careful not to burn.
Add cooked gnocchi and roasted cherry tomatoes to the skillet with sage butter. Gently toss to coat. Serve immediately. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Shrimp and Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: The Cajun Shrimp and Vegetable Rice is presented as a generous, vibrant mound on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is a rich reddish-brown from the tomato paste and spices, flecked with bright, contrasting colors. Plump, orange-pink cooked shrimp are nestled throughout, their curves catching the light. Diced red and green bell peppers, orange carrots, and pale green squash cubes are visibly tender-crisp, adding texture and color bursts. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped green onions or parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The dish is inviting and hearty, with a slightly saucy, cohesive texture. Moderate negative space surrounds the central dish. The setting features a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of hot sauce (e.g., Tabasco) for individual adjustment.
Often accompanied by cornbread or French bread to soak up the juices.

ingredients.name: Bell peppers (red and green), diced 1 cm cubes
Fresh parsley or green onions, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion, bell peppers, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in diced carrot and squash. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic, tomato paste, Cajun seasoning, smoked paprika, dried thyme, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, ensuring it is well coated with the spice mixture.
Pour in chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover the pot tightly and simmer for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Add shrimp to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Cover and cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until shrimp are pink and cooked through and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley or green onions before serving.
notes: For added depth, you can brown 150g of diced Andouille sausage or smoked sausage before adding the "holy trinity" in step 2. Remove sausage, then add back in step 8 with the shrimp.
Adjust cayenne pepper to control spice level.
Ensure rice is not stirred excessively during simmering to prevent stickiness.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing the "holy trinity" (onions, bell peppers, celery) as a flavor base
Developing a rich, savory "gravy" within the rice dish

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Italian Sausage with Roasted Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two pan-seared Italian sausages, cooked whole, resting beside a mound of golden-brown roasted rosemary potatoes on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The sausages exhibit a rich, caramelized crust with a savory aroma, while the potatoes are cut into 2 cm chunks, their exteriors crisp and interiors fluffy, lightly coated with finely chopped rosemary. A light, glossy pan sauce, enriched with chicken broth and butter, is drizzled artistically over and around the sausages. The overall composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti or Sangiovese
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks.
Toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, finely chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 30-35 minutes. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
While potatoes roast, heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausages to the hot skillet. Sear until browned on all sides. This takes about 8-10 minutes.
Transfer skillet with sausages to the oven for the last 15 minutes of potato roasting. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove sausages from skillet. Keep warm.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pan.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter until melted. This creates a pan sauce.
Serve sausages and potatoes with the pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust roasting time for potatoes based on desired crispness.
Ensure sausages reach an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion Tart Tatin
recipes.visual_description: A single wedge of Caramelized Onion Tart Tatin is presented on a round, off-white ceramic dessert plate. The top layer features deeply caramelized, thinly sliced onions, showcasing rich amber and golden-brown hues. The onions are glossy and slightly sticky, arranged organically. Beneath, the puff pastry is golden, flaky, and visibly puffed, forming a crisp base. A small scoop of creamy vanilla bean ice cream or a dollop of crème fraîche rests beside the tart, its smooth texture contrasting with the tart's complexity. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal dessert fork and a casually folded linen napkin complete the homely, relaxed French setting. Warm, soft lighting highlights the dessert's comforting appeal. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with vanilla bean ice cream or a dollop of crème fraîche.
Enjoy with a small glass of dessert wine.
instructions: Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet (approx. 20 cm diameter) over medium-low heat.
Add thinly sliced onions. Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Onions should be very soft and translucent.
Increase heat to medium. Add sugar. Cook, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes. Sugar will melt and caramelize with the onions.
Stir in balsamic vinegar. Cook for 2 more minutes. Remove skillet from heat.
Arrange caramelized onions evenly in the skillet.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Roll out puff pastry slightly larger than the skillet. Place pastry over the onions, tucking the edges down around the sides.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Pastry should be golden brown and puffed.
Carefully remove from oven. Let cool for 5 minutes.
Place a serving plate over the skillet. Carefully invert the tart onto the plate.
Serve warm.
notes: Use a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet that can go directly from stovetop to oven.
Be careful when caramelizing the sugar; it can burn quickly.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and White Bean Paella
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish paella is presented in a traditional, wide, shallow paella pan. The golden saffron-infused Bomba rice forms the base, cooked to a fluid, slightly al dente consistency, with a desirable crispy 'socarrat' layer visible at the bottom edges. Nestled within the rice are generously sized, browned chunks of seared chicken thigh, providing a robust focal point. Bright orange diced carrots, deep red diced bell pepper, and creamy white beans are evenly distributed throughout, adding contrasting colors and textures. A scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green flat-leaf parsley adorns the top. Lemon wedges are artfully placed on the rim of the pan, ready for squeezing. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a clean white porcelain dinner plate and a cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, authentic Spanish culinary scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan for a communal dining experience.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up the flavorful juices.
Offer additional lemon wedges for guests to squeeze over their portions.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Dice onion, carrots (1cm cubes), and red bell pepper (1cm cubes). Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a 30cm paella pan or large, shallow oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Add chicken to the pan. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and red bell pepper to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in undrained diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Steep saffron threads in 50ml of hot chicken broth.
Stir in rice until coated with the tomato mixture. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in remaining hot chicken broth and saffron-infused broth. Stir gently once to distribute ingredients.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir the rice during this time.
Rinse and drain white beans. Gently stir in white beans during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Increase heat to medium-high for the last 2-3 minutes to create a 'socarrat' (crispy bottom layer of rice). Listen for crackling sounds. Do not burn.
Remove from heat. Cover pan loosely with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Chop fresh flat-leaf parsley. Cut lemon into wedges.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges. Serve directly from the pan.
notes: Do not stir the rice excessively during cooking; this releases starch and prevents the desired 'socarrat' (crispy bottom).
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Arroz y Maíz Picante
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. A single portion of Pollo con Arroz y Maíz Picante sits neatly. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4cm, are nestled amongst vibrant yellow rice. The rice is studded with bright green peas and yellow corn kernels. Diced red bell pepper and onion are visible, adding specks of color. A light scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the top. The textures are varied: tender chicken, fluffy rice, and slightly crisp vegetables. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, dominated by the rich yellow of the rice and chicken, contrasted by the green of peas and cilantro. A lime wedge is placed on the side of the plate for a touch of freshness. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm corn tortillas.
Offer a simple green salad with a lime vinaigrette.
Accompany with a small bowl of hot sauce or salsa picante.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and Dijon mustard. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pot. Stir to coat rice with vegetable mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in corn kernels and green peas. Continue to simmer, covered, for 5-7 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Chicken and Brown Rice Casserole
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Baked Chicken and Brown Rice Casserole is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The casserole is scooped naturally onto the plate, showcasing its hearty, comforting texture. Diced, tender chicken pieces are visible throughout, mixed with soft, cooked brown rice, vibrant diced carrots, and earthy sliced mushrooms. A golden-brown, melted layer of cheddar cheese tops the casserole, with some cheese visibly incorporated into the mix. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color and freshness. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A standard metal fork rests beside the plate, completing the casual, homely setting. The scene captures a relaxed family dining atmosphere, focusing on the wholesome, inviting appearance of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
Serve with crusty bread for soaking up juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced carrots, and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften.
Stir in uncooked brown rice and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Stir to combine.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Check chicken internal temperature to ensure it reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Stir in half of the shredded cheese until melted.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the top. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust liquid amount if brown rice seems too dry or too wet after baking; different brands absorb liquid differently.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Potato, Corn, and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: This dish features tender, braised chicken thighs nestled amidst chunky vegetables in a rich, savory sauce. A single, golden-brown chicken thigh, its skin lightly crisped from initial searing, is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain plate. Around it, generous chunks of roasted potato, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and diced red tomatoes are artfully arranged, showcasing their natural shapes and colors. The dark, glossy beef stock-based sauce pools around the ingredients, hinting at its depth of flavor. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white linen napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.

ingredients.name: Waxy potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold), cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side. Remove chicken; set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits. Cook until almost evaporated.
Stir in diced tomatoes, beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Continue simmering, covered, for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir in corn kernels. Cook for 5 minutes more, uncovered, to allow sauce to thicken slightly.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Baked Beef and Mozzarella Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty baked beef and mozzarella pasta is served in a sturdy, light-colored ceramic bowl with a slightly imperfect rim. The pasta is coated in a rich, reddish-brown sauce, with crumbled browned ground beef, diced bell pepper, diced onion, and sliced mushrooms visible throughout. Melted mozzarella cheese forms a golden-brown, bubbly crust on top, with some delicious stretches of cheese. Fresh basil leaves are scattered casually over the surface, adding a pop of green. The bowl sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. Beside the bowl, a simple everyday fork and knife are placed, and a casually folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone rests nearby. A slice of golden-brown garlic bread leans against the side of the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen setting with minimal, natural clutter in the background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
While pasta cooks, prepare garlic bread. Mix softened butter with garlic powder. Spread on bread slices. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pot. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 3-4 minutes until fragrant and mushrooms soften.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, dried oregano, beef broth, salt, pepper, and optional sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir cooked pasta and fresh chopped basil into the sauce. Mix well to combine.
Transfer half of the pasta mixture to a 20x30cm baking dish.
Sprinkle half of the mozzarella cheese over the pasta.
Add the remaining pasta mixture. Top with the remaining mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and lightly golden.
During the last 10 minutes of baking, toast garlic bread in the oven or a toaster oven until golden.
Remove pasta from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with extra fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Root Vegetable & Lentil Ragu Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of al dente rigatoni, lightly coated in a rich, earthy lentil ragu, is presented centrally on a round, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. Scattered around and within the pasta are roasted root vegetable chunks (carrots, parsnips, celery root), retaining their natural, slightly caramelized edges. The ragu is a deep reddish-brown, with visible green lentils and finely minced aromatics. Bright, finely diced pieces of preserved lemon peel are subtly mixed throughout, adding a pop of yellow. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered on top. The composition is clean and uncrowded, with ample white space on the plate. The plate rests on a light-colored, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the textures of the pasta and vegetables. The background is a clean, minimalist off-white wall with a hint of green from a blurred houseplant.
instructions: Rinse lentils. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced carrots, parsnips, and celery root with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add minced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 30-35 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Stir occasionally.
While ragu cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni pasta. Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Stir finely diced preserved lemon and nutritional yeast into the lentil ragu. If ragu is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Add cooked pasta to the ragu. Toss to combine.
Gently fold in roasted root vegetables.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by encouraging the use of vegetable scraps (peels, ends) to make the vegetable broth.
The use of preserved lemon incorporates a fermentation technique, adding depth and complexity with minimal waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Tofu Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Tofu Stir-fry is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim. The stir-fry is piled naturally in the center, showing an inviting mix of colors and textures. Golden-brown, crispy tofu cubes are interspersed with vibrant green broccoli florets, bright orange carrot rounds, and slender red bell pepper strips, all coated in a glossy, savory brown sauce. The vegetables are tender-crisp, maintaining their distinct shapes and natural hues. The tofu pieces are clearly defined, showing their textured surface. A small sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adds a subtle visual pop. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. Alongside, a small bowl of fluffy white steamed rice and a pair of wooden chopsticks rest casually. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed white rice.
Offer a small dish of chili garlic sauce or sriracha on the side for those who prefer extra heat.
Present with a simple broth or clear soup as a starter.
instructions: Press tofu. Wrap tofu block in paper towels. Place between two plates. Add a heavy weight on top. Press for 30 minutes to remove excess water.
Cut tofu. Cut pressed tofu into 2 cm cubes.

Crisp tofu. Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes in a single layer. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu and set aside.
Prepare sauce. Whisk together soy sauce, vegetable broth, cornstarch, brown sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Set aside.
Stir-fry aromatics. Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the same wok. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir-fry vegetables. Add broccoli florets and carrot rounds. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add red bell pepper strips and snap peas. Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.

Combine. Return crispy tofu to the wok with vegetables. Stir the prepared sauce. Pour sauce over tofu and vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately.
notes: Pressing tofu is crucial for achieving crispy texture. Do not skip this step.
Adjust the sweetness or saltiness of the sauce to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Shrimp with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A modest, individual portion of Creamy Garlic Shrimp with Rice is presented in a simple, deep, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. Fluffy white long-grain rice, with its individual grains distinct, forms a comforting base. Several whole, plump, pink shrimp, naturally curled from cooking, are nestled generously on top of the rice. Each shrimp is coated in a velvety, pale cream-colored garlic sauce that glistens invitingly, pooling slightly around the rice. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is abundantly scattered over the shrimp and sauce, providing a vibrant, natural contrast. The shallots in the sauce are finely diced, and the garlic is minced. The setting suggests a homely family kitchen, with soft, cozy lighting creating a relaxed atmosphere. A basic, everyday metal spoon rests casually beside the bowl. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in dining area.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 600 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Keep warm.
Pat shrimp dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced shallots. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add seasoned shrimp to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from pan and set aside.
Pour chicken stock into the pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce heat slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Return cooked shrimp to the sauce. Stir to coat. Add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, if desired.
Ladle rice into individual bowls. Top with creamy garlic shrimp. Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty beef stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, browned beef chunks, soft, chunky potatoes, and vibrant orange carrot pieces nestled in a rich, dark brown, slightly glossy gravy. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, unpretentious look. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a functional garnish and a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table with visible grain. Beside the bowl, a simple, off-white ceramic plate holds a slice of crusty bread. A plain, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone and a sturdy, everyday metal fork are casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam gently rising from the stew. The background hints at a lived-in kitchen, slightly blurred, maintaining focus on the food. Beef chuck is cut into 3-4 cm cubes, carrots into 2 cm chunks, and potatoes into 3 cm chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to cook off raw flour taste.
Pour in red wine (if using) and beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add dried thyme and bay leaves.
Add potatoes. Ensure liquid covers most ingredients. Add more broth if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Cook on low heat for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, brown the beef well in batches.
Stew can be made ahead and reheats well. Flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro with Crispy Garlic Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting mound of spaghetti, perfectly coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. The spaghetti is twirled naturally on a simple, round ceramic plate, allowing some strands to fall casually. A scattering of golden, crispy garlic breadcrumbs (pangrattato) tops the pasta, providing textural contrast. A few fresh green basil leaves are torn and sprinkled over, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese is optional. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin, perhaps a checkered pattern, is casually placed next to the plate. A rustic fork is beside the plate. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy kitchen or dining area. The background is slightly blurred, showing hints of a simple home kitchen, perhaps a salt and pepper shaker or a small glass of water. A single, modest, home-style portion is presented.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the leftover sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Prepare Breadcrumbs: Tear stale bread into small pieces. Process in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.

Toast Breadcrumbs: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add breadcrumbs. Toast, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Season with salt and pepper. Remove breadcrumbs from pan. Set aside.
Make Tomato Sauce: In the same pan, add remaining 30 ml olive oil. Heat over medium-low heat. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add crushed tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cook Pasta: While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

Combine: Before draining pasta, reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water. Drain spaghetti. Add cooked spaghetti directly to the tomato sauce. Add half of the fresh basil leaves, torn. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Toss well to coat pasta.
Serve: Divide pasta among 4 individual plates. Top each portion generously with the crispy garlic breadcrumbs. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves, torn. Serve immediately.
notes: Using good quality canned tomatoes makes a big difference.
The breadcrumbs add a wonderful texture and can be prepared ahead of time.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Beef Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Potato and Beef Salad is presented on an everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features warm, halved baby potatoes with their skins on, mixed with vibrant green beans, bright red halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced purple-red onion. Small, rustic chunks of seared beef are nestled among the vegetables. The ingredients are casually tossed and lightly coated in a creamy, golden Dijon vinaigrette, allowing natural colors and textures to shine. A sprinkling of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color. The plating is unpretentious, with components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, comfort food style. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal.
instructions: Wash baby potatoes. Halve or quarter larger potatoes. Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Trim ends off green beans. Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Drain and immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Pat beef sirloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear steak for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Remove steak from skillet, rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes. Dice beef into 1.5 cm cubes.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion.
Chop fresh parsley.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in 5 tablespoons olive oil, whisking constantly until emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, combine warm potatoes, blanched green beans, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion. Add diced beef.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat everything evenly.
Stir in chopped parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Negro con Pan Tostado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo en Mole Negro is presented on a clean, round white ceramic plate. Two generous chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on, are centrally placed, fully coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce is thick but flows naturally, pooling around the chicken pieces. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh cilantro and a scattering of toasted golden sesame seeds garnish the top of the chicken and sauce. Beside the chicken, two slices of golden-brown, rustic toasted bread are neatly arranged. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the deep colors of the mole and the crispy texture of the toasted bread. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, with a small, traditional Mexican ceramic bowl, perhaps holding a side of pickled onions, in the background, adding cultural context without distracting from the main dish. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice
Offer crema or queso fresco on the side

ingredients.name: Unsweetened dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher)
Stale crusty bread (e.g., bolillo or baguette), sliced 2 cm thick

instructions: Wipe chiles clean. Toast chiles in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Remove stems and seeds. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Soak for 20 minutes until softened. Drain chiles, reserve soaking liquid.

Heat lard in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.

Add onion and garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add almonds, sesame seeds, raisins, cinnamon stick, cloves, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, and oregano. Toast spices for 2 minutes until fragrant.

Add roasted tomatoes, softened chiles, and 200 ml of chicken broth to the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes. Transfer mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth, adding more chicken broth or reserved chile soaking liquid if needed. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing solids.
Return strained sauce to the pot. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Stir in chocolate and sugar. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens. Season with salt to taste.
Return seared chicken thighs to the mole sauce. Ensure chicken is submerged. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, toast bread slices. Lightly brush bread with oil. Toast in a pan or oven until golden brown and crispy.
Serve chicken with ample mole sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and toasted sesame seeds. Serve with toasted bread on the side.
notes: Mole sauce improves in flavor the day after it's made. Prepare it in advance for best results.
The straining step is crucial for a smooth, velvety mole sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro with Crispy Pangrattato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant spaghetti is artfully coiled in the center of a clean, white round porcelain plate, presenting a refined yet approachable look. The pasta is coated in a rich, red tomato sauce, showcasing visible pieces of bright red tomato and flecks of green basil. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown, irregular crispy pangrattato covers the top, providing a textural contrast. The spaghetti is arranged in a moderate mound, allowing for appropriate negative space around the edges of the plate. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are neatly arranged beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional fresh basil leaves on the side.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
A basket of crusty bread for dipping in any remaining sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Prepare tomatoes: Score a small 'X' on the bottom of each tomato. Blanch tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds. Transfer to an ice bath. Peel, core, and roughly chop tomatoes.

Make pangrattato: Tear bread into small pieces. Pulse in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Add 2 minced garlic cloves during the last minute of cooking. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Start sauce: Heat 50 ml olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, do not brown garlic.

Add tomatoes: Add chopped tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook pasta: While sauce simmers, cook spaghetti in a large pot of generously salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Combine: Transfer drained spaghetti directly into the tomato sauce. Add half of the reserved pasta water and toss vigorously to emulsify the sauce and coat the pasta. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Finish: Stir in fresh basil leaves, torn.
Serve: Divide spaghetti among four plates. Garnish generously with crispy pangrattato. Offer grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
notes: Using ripe, high-quality tomatoes is crucial for the sauce's flavor.
The pasta cooking water helps emulsify the sauce and create a silky texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Dijon Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a rich golden-brown from searing, with visible flecks of black pepper. A glossy, pale yellow Dijon cream sauce is generously spooned over and around the chicken, creating a smooth, inviting pool. Small, vibrant green fresh thyme leaves are suspended within the sauce. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley rests atop the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken is presented whole, showing its plump form. The plating is organized and professional, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, casual bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple steamed green beans or roasted potato wedges.
Offer crusty French baguette for dipping into the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Add chicken breasts to the skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is reached. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside on a plate, tented with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 3-4 minutes.
Whisk in Dijon mustard until well combined. Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, spooning sauce over them. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and White Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant Mediterranean palette. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thigh, cooked to a tender finish, sits prominently at the center. Its surface shows subtle char marks and a sprinkle of vibrant green fresh oregano leaves. Alongside the chicken, a neat mound of roasted new potato halves displays a crispy, golden-brown skin and a soft, inviting interior. The potatoes are irregularly shaped, showcasing their natural form. Adjacent to the potatoes, a generous scoop of white bean salad bursts with color: creamy white cannellini beans are interspersed with bright red halved cherry tomatoes, vibrant green small-cubed cucumber, thin translucent slices of red onion, and dark, glossy black Kalamata olive halves. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered throughout the salad, adding a textural contrast. The entire composition is lightly drizzled with olive oil, creating a subtle sheen. Fresh green sprigs of oregano are strategically placed on the chicken and salad for aromatic and visual garnish. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests near the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and fresh colors of the ingredients, creating an appealing, professional bistro-style presentation with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread for dipping in the juices.
Offer extra lemon wedges on the side for individual preference.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, half juiced, half cut into wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. In a large bowl, toss halved potatoes with 30ml olive oil, half of the chopped fresh oregano, rosemary, thyme, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, toss chicken with 20ml olive oil, remaining chopped fresh oregano, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.

After 25 minutes, add seared chicken thighs to the baking sheet with the potatoes. Return to oven. Continue roasting for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
While chicken and potatoes finish, combine rinsed cannellini beans, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, and halved Kalamata olives in a medium bowl.
Drizzle the white bean salad with 30ml olive oil and fresh lemon juice. Add crumbled feta cheese. Gently toss to combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Place a roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange a portion of roasted potatoes alongside. Spoon a generous serving of the white bean salad next to the potatoes.
Garnish with fresh oregano sprigs and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is elegantly presented on a round, matte white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared and roasted boneless chicken thighs, each tender and glistening, are positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant, roasted vegetables: several bright red, plump cherry tomatoes, thick-cut planks of tender-crisp zucchini with slight char marks, and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. A light, savory pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh sprigs of green oregano and thyme, along with a bright yellow lemon wedge, are placed strategically as a garnish, adding color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness.
Roasted potatoes or couscous can be served on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large oven-safe skillet, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add minced garlic, cherry tomatoes, zucchini planks, and red onion wedges. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté vegetables for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Return chicken to the skillet, nesting it among the vegetables.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, chopped oregano, chopped thyme, and chicken broth.
Pour mixture over chicken and vegetables in the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the skillet for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly cooked to 75°C (167°F) for safety.
Do not overcrowd the skillet during searing to ensure proper browning.
Adjust herbs based on personal preference; fresh is highly recommended for flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Sticky Rice with Coconut Corn Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of sweet sticky rice is artfully plated on a clean, round white porcelain plate, forming a neat mound. The rice, steamed to tender consistency, gleams from coconut milk infusion. Beside it, a generous dollop of golden-yellow coconut corn cream is elegantly placed, showcasing vibrant kernels. Thin slices of fresh, ripe mango are carefully arranged alongside, adding a pop of bright orange.
