Beside the rice, two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cut into thick, irregular chunks (not fanned), are nestled, showcasing their crisp, caramelized exterior. Vibrant, thinly sliced pickled red bell pepper and translucent pickled red onion are artfully arranged alongside the chicken and rice, adding pops of natural color and delicate texture. A scattering of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley provides a minimal, natural green accent. The composition is clean, balanced, and unforced, emphasizing the inherent beauty of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly folded nearby. Soft, diffused natural lighting illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows. A hint of green foliage from a plant is visible in the clean, minimalist background, completing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Place in a clean jar with 750 ml filtered water and 5 g sea salt. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours. Drain well before cooking.
Thinly slice red bell pepper and red onion. Set aside.
Prepare pickling brine: Combine 1 litre water, 250 ml white wine vinegar, 15 g sea salt, and 10 g sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Stir until salt and sugar dissolve. Remove from heat.
Pour hot brine over sliced bell pepper and onion in a heatproof jar. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Cook fermented rice: Combine drained rice with 600 ml fresh water or chicken stock in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Cut rested chicken thighs into thick, irregular chunks.
To plate, spoon a mound of fermented rice onto each plate. Arrange chicken chunks alongside the rice. Drain pickled bell pepper and onion slices and artfully place them next to the chicken.
Garnish with freshly chopped chives or parsley.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by encouraging the use of vegetable scraps (onion peels, bell pepper cores) and chicken bones for homemade stock, which can be used to cook the rice or for other dishes.
Fermentation of rice enhances its digestibility and adds a subtle tangy depth to the dish, aligning with sustainable food practices.
Adjust pickling brine sweetness and acidity to your preference. The pickled vegetables can be made several days in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Apple Potato Hash and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken with Apple Potato Hash and Tomato Confit is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The boneless chicken thigh, with its crisp, golden-brown skin, is the focal point, resting on a bed of golden-brown apple potato hash. The hash features small cubes of tender potato and apple, mixed with subtle green flecks of herbs. Scattered around the chicken and hash are vibrant, deep red confit cherry tomatoes, some whole and some gently burst, glistening with olive oil. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the varying textures: the crispy chicken skin, the tender chicken meat, the soft burst tomatoes, and the tender-crisp hash. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard, clean flatware are placed beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, ensuring the dish remains the primary focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip chicken.
Add 50ml chicken broth to the skillet. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast chicken for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

While chicken roasts, prepare tomato confit. Place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven alongside the chicken for 15-20 minutes, until tomatoes are softened and slightly wrinkled.
For the hash, heat remaining 30ml olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add small diced potatoes to the skillet. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and lightly browned.
Add small diced apples, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and thyme to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until apples soften slightly.
Stir in apple cider vinegar. Season hash with salt and pepper to taste.

To plate, spoon a portion of apple potato hash onto each white porcelain dinner plate. Place a roasted chicken thigh atop the hash. Arrange confit cherry tomatoes around the chicken and hash. Garnish with a fresh herb sprig if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken and Black Bean Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Mexican Chicken and Black Bean Skillet is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features succulent, pan-seared chicken chunks, approximately 2.5 cm in size, mixed with tender black beans, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and diced red and green bell peppers. The ingredients are naturally combined, some overlapping, creating a rustic and comforting appearance. A generous sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro provides a pop of green. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with rich browns from the chicken, dark purples from the beans, and bright yellows and reds from the vegetables. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, allowing for some negative space. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with a stack of warm corn tortillas in a simple woven basket and a few lime wedges scattered beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy family dining atmosphere. A casually placed plain linen napkin completes the homely feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or rice.
Offer salsa or a dollop of sour cream on the side.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes until browned on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the same skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add drained black beans, drained corn, and chicken broth. Stir to combine.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to slightly thicken.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the fresh cilantro.
Serve hot with remaining cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Cucumber Salad with Herb Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. Natural light from a nearby window illuminates the dish. The salad features a vibrant mix of diced red tomatoes and green cucumber, with thin slivers of red onion interspersed. Small, irregular chunks of pan-cooked chicken, displaying a light golden-brown sear, are scattered throughout the vegetables, not dominating the visual. Fresh green parsley is generously chopped and mixed in, adding flecks of bright color. A light vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them together. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from a family kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and standard cutlery are casually placed beside the bowl.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of olive oil.
Cook chicken breast for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Let chicken rest 5 minutes. Cut chicken into 2 cm chunks.
Dice tomatoes into 2 cm pieces.
Dice cucumber into 1.5 cm pieces.
Thinly slice red onion. Separate onion rings.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, and chopped parsley.
Add chicken chunks to the vegetables.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single individual portion. A generous mound of al dente fettuccine, coated in a creamy, pale ivory sauce, forms the base. Nestled within and around the pasta are succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks, each about 2.5 cm in size, showing a slight char from searing. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. The sauce has a smooth, rich consistency, lightly clinging to the pasta strands. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish on top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add cooked chicken chunks to the sauce. Stir to combine.
Add drained fettuccine to the pan with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Do not overcook pasta; it should be al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Herbed Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The 'Roasted Tomato and Herbed Rice Salad' is presented in a large, slightly rustic ceramic serving bowl, typical of home kitchenware. The colors are vibrant and natural: deep red, slightly burst roasted tomatoes, alongside fluffy white rice, crisp green cucumber cubes, and delicate purple-red rings of thinly sliced red onion. A creamy, pale green herb dressing lightly coats all components, showing specks of fresh parsley. The salad is loosely mounded, allowing ingredients to naturally intermingle and slightly overlap, creating a comforting, bountiful appearance. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, slightly rumpled linen napkin beside it. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family meal. A fork with a few strands of rice and a tomato piece rests near the bowl.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

While tomatoes roast, cook rice. Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice and 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 60ml olive oil, white wine vinegar, milk, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, 15g chopped parsley, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked rice, roasted tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and diced cucumber. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Garnish with remaining chopped parsley. Serve immediately or chill.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Black Bean Skillet
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing a generous, comforting portion. Diced chicken, seared to a golden-brown, is nestled among plump, dark black beans and fluffy, seasoned rice. Interspersed throughout are softened, vibrant red and green bell pepper pieces and translucent diced onion, adding pops of color. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro provides a fragrant, natural garnish on top. The textures are varied: tender chicken, creamy beans, and distinct rice grains. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with earthy browns, deep blacks, and fresh green accents. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table with a casual, lived-in feel. A simple cloth napkin is casually draped beside it, and a lime wedge is placed on the rim of the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene from above.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a side of salsa or sour cream.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed black beans and uncooked rice.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: This is a one-pan meal, great for weeknights.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork with Savory Mushroom Rice and Quick-Fermented Red Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Braised Pork with Savory Mushroom Rice is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Two to three substantial, tender braised pork chunks, their surfaces glistening with rich brown braising liquid, are placed alongside a neat, fluffy mound of savory mushroom rice. A vibrant red quick-fermented red onion relish is spooned over the pork, adding a bright pop of color and crisp texture. A small, fresh cluster of vibrant green arugula or microgreens garnishes the dish, providing a touch of freshness. The overall composition is clean, minimalistic, and showcases natural textures. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural light, emphasizing sustainability and the inherent beauty of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Cremini mushrooms
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, caps finely chopped, stems roughly chopped

ingredients.name: Vegetable stock
ingredients.quantity: 500 ml (use homemade from scraps or store-bought)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat pork chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork from pot.
Add diced yellow onions, diced red bell pepper, and 4 crushed garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return pork to pot. Add vegetable stock and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot and braise in the preheated oven for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.
While pork braises, prepare mushroom base for rice: Sauté roughly chopped mushroom stems and 2 minced garlic cloves in a separate pan until browned and tender. Set aside.

Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rinsed rice with 600 ml water in a saucepan. Add half of the sautéed mushroom stem and garlic mixture. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Make quick-fermented red onion relish: In a small bowl or jar, combine thinly sliced red onion with 200 ml warm water, 5 g salt, 5 g sugar, and apple cider vinegar. Stir until salt and sugar dissolve. Let sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour, or refrigerate for longer fermentation.
Remove pork from braising liquid. Reduce braising liquid on stovetop over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Skim any excess fat.

To plate, spoon a mound of savory mushroom rice onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 braised pork chunks next to the rice. Spoon quick-fermented red onion relish over the pork. Garnish with fresh arugula or microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage and Apple Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. Its minimalistic composition highlights natural beauty. Finely shredded, pale green fermented cabbage forms the base, contrasting with vibrant, thin slices of green apple. Apple slices are cut into precise crescents or small batons, adding crisp texture. Golden-brown toasted pumpkin seeds are scattered generously, providing warm color and crunch. Bright green dill sprigs offer a pop of color and freshness. The dressing lightly coats ingredients, adding a subtle sheen. Ample negative space enhances the clean aesthetic. The setting includes a light reclaimed wood table and undyed linen napkin, under soft natural light.
instructions: Remove outer leaves from cabbage. Reserve for other uses. Shred remaining cabbage finely. Place shredded cabbage in a large bowl. Add sea salt. Massage cabbage with salt for 5-7 minutes until it releases liquid and softens.

Pack cabbage tightly into a clean glass jar. Pour released liquid over cabbage to submerge. If not enough liquid, add a little salted water to cover. Weigh down cabbage to keep it submerged. Cover jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Taste daily until desired tanginess. Store fermented cabbage in the refrigerator.
Core and thinly slice the green apple.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Add pumpkin seeds. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring often, until golden and fragrant. Remove from pan.
In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, and water (or 30 ml reserved cabbage fermentation liquid).
In a large bowl, combine fermented cabbage and sliced apple. Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh dill sprigs.
notes: Emphasizes using fermentation for flavor and preservation. This recipe minimizes waste by utilizing the full cabbage and creating a dressing with natural byproducts.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage, Broccoli Rabe, and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: The Orecchiette with Italian Sausage, Broccoli Rabe, and Ricotta is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl. Perfectly al dente orecchiette pasta is tossed with browned, crumbled Italian sausage and vibrant green, coarsely chopped broccoli rabe. The ingredients are integrated naturally, not overly arranged. Creamy dollops of fresh, white ricotta cheese are placed atop the pasta, melting slightly into the warm dish. A light dusting of grated Pecorino Romano cheese and fresh, finely chopped parsley sprigs garnish the plate. The composition features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's rich colors and varied textures. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, alongside a traditional silver fork and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the inviting, authentic Italian presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese
instructions: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Add broccoli rabe. Cook for 2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Transfer broccoli rabe to an ice bath immediately to stop cooking. Drain well. Coarsely chop the blanched broccoli rabe.

Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook until browned and cooked through. Break up any large pieces with a spoon. Drain excess fat from the skillet. Remove cooked sausage from the skillet and set aside.

Add 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic. Add the coarsely chopped broccoli rabe to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and black pepper.

While the broccoli rabe cooks, add orecchiette pasta to the same pot of salted boiling water used for the broccoli rabe. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml of the pasta cooking water before draining the pasta.

Return the cooked sausage to the skillet with the broccoli rabe. Add the drained orecchiette pasta and chicken broth. Add 125ml of the reserved pasta water. Toss all ingredients to combine thoroughly. Simmer for 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.

Remove the skillet from heat. Stir in 40g of grated Pecorino Romano cheese. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately. Dollop fresh ricotta cheese generously over each serving. Garnish with remaining Pecorino Romano and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cola-Glazed Chicken Thighs with Hot Milk Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a succulent, bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, deeply golden and crisp from searing, coated in a glistening, sticky, dark reddish-brown cola glaze. The chicken is placed centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A rich, thick pool of the spicy cola glaze gathers around the base of the chicken. Around the chicken and glaze, a delicate, airy hot milk emulsion, light off-white in color, is artfully drizzled, adding a contrasting creamy texture. Small, vibrant green flecks of finely chopped fresh chives are sprinkled over the chicken and emulsion, providing a fresh aromatic counterpoint. The chicken itself shows clear evidence of proper cooking, with a taut, caramelized skin and hints of tender meat beneath. The plate maintains moderate negative space. It sits on a simple wooden table surface. A grey cotton napkin and basic metal flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred casual restaurant background. The entire plate is visible.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side.
In a bowl, whisk together Coca-Cola, hot sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.
Remove skillet from heat. Carefully drain excess fat, leaving about 15 ml. Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the vodka. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Pour in the Coca-Cola glaze mixture. Bring to a simmer.

Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Baste chicken occasionally with the glaze.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Place skillet with remaining glaze on stovetop over medium heat. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until glaze thickens to a syrupy consistency.

While chicken rests, heat milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until warm but not boiling. Whisk in butter and a pinch of hot sauce (optional, for extra kick). Use an immersion blender or whisk vigorously to create a light foam/emulsion.
Place a chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amount of thickened cola glaze over chicken. Drizzle hot milk emulsion around the chicken. Garnish with chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For a leaner option, boneless, skinless chicken thighs can be used, but adjust searing and baking times as they will cook faster. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast positioned slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, exhibits a beautifully caramelized crust and retains its natural shape. A rich, creamy mushroom sauce, studded with sliced browned cremini mushrooms and fresh thyme, is generously spooned over and around the chicken. Beside the chicken, a vibrant bundle of roasted asparagus spears, slightly charred at the tips, adds a contrasting green color and textural element. The plate has moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate on a simple wooden table. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, modern bistro atmosphere. No fanned slices of meat are present. The chicken is presented as a whole piece.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss asparagus with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest.
Add remaining 15 g butter to the skillet. Add minced shallot and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic and thyme leaves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook for 2 minutes until wine is mostly reduced.
Stir in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Return chicken breasts to the skillet, spooning sauce over them. Serve immediately with roasted asparagus.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after searing helps keep it juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is free-flowing and spread naturally. Its vibrant orange-red hue contrasts with golden-brown seared chicken chunks, interspersed throughout. Halved, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and texture. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, providing a pale yellow accent. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as garnish, offering a pop of green. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 15 g, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 10 minutes, add halved cherry tomatoes to the risotto. Continue cooking and stirring.
When rice is al dente (creamy but with a slight bite), remove from heat.
Stir in cooked chicken, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter. Stir vigorously for 1 minute for mantecatura (creamy finish).
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring for optimal creaminess.
Ensure broth is hot for continuous cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Orzo and Cannellini Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, braised chicken thigh rests on a bed of al dente orzo pasta on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce, generously studded with vibrant green and red bell pepper chunks, softened onion, and creamy white cannellini beans. The sauce has a glossy sheen, indicating its depth. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the well-proportioned elements. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. In the background, a small rustic bowl of grated Parmesan cheese and a basket of crusty Italian bread enhance the casual bistro atmosphere. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer a side of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
While chicken simmers, cook orzo pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir drained cannellini beans into the chicken sauce during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken cacciatore over orzo pasta. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best flavor, use good quality canned tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Garlic Basil Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Garlic Basil Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on an off-white, slightly textured ceramic dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh rests prominently. Beside it, a generous, casual pile of roasted potato wedges, golden and fluffy, are scattered naturally. The chicken is whole. The potatoes are rustic wedges. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are loosely tossed among the chicken and potatoes, some slightly wilted, adding pops of color. The arrangement is asymmetrical and home-style. The plate is on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, silver fork and knife are casually laid beside the plate. A loosely folded, beige cloth napkin sits nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture creates a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic 2.5 cm wedges.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, minced garlic, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Immediately toss chicken and potatoes with remaining 30ml olive oil and fresh basil leaves. The residual heat will slightly wilt the basil.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Lentil & Sausage Croquettes with Quick Fermented Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of modern, sustainable cuisine is presented on a natural, light beige ceramic plate with a matte finish. Four to five golden-brown Lentil & Sausage Croquettes, approximately 5 cm long and 3 cm wide, are arranged organically in the center, showing their crisp, textured exterior. Their shapes are naturally irregular, emphasizing their handcrafted quality. A vibrant mound of Quick Fermented Cabbage Slaw, showcasing thinly shredded white cabbage and julienned orange carrots, is placed alongside the croquettes, adding a fresh, slightly tangy contrast. The slaw is lightly dressed, retaining its natural volume and texture. A creamy, off-white dollop of Herb Cheese Dip, subtly speckled with finely chopped green chives and dill, sits adjacent, offering a rich, savory counterpoint. The dish is garnished simply with a few small, fresh dill sprigs scattered over the croquettes and slaw. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin is subtly placed. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients against a clean, minimalist background with a hint of green from a potted plant.

ingredients.name: Plain Greek yogurt or sour cream

instructions: Prepare Quick Fermented Cabbage Slaw: In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, julienned carrot, dill, mint, and parsley. Sprinkle with sea salt. Massage the cabbage mixture vigorously with your hands for 5-7 minutes until it softens and releases liquid. Stir in apple cider vinegar. Pack tightly into a clean jar or container. Let sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour.
Cook Lentils: Rinse lentils. In a saucepan, combine lentils and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid.

Prepare Sausage Mixture: In a large pan, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant. Add sausage meat, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain any excess fat.

Form Croquettes: In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, cooked sausage mixture, breadcrumbs, and beaten egg. Mix well until combined. Season with salt and pepper. Form the mixture into 16-20 small oval or round croquettes, about 4-5 cm in length.

Cook Croquettes: Heat the remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Place croquettes in the pan in batches. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crisp. Alternatively, bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.

Make Herb Cheese Dip: In a small bowl, combine crumbled feta cheese, Greek yogurt, olive oil, chives, dill, and lemon zest. Mash with a fork until well combined and slightly creamy. Season with black pepper.
Serve: Arrange 4-5 croquettes per plate. Serve alongside a generous portion of the quick fermented cabbage slaw and a dollop of the herb cheese dip.
notes: The quick fermented slaw provides a tangy, probiotic element, enhancing the dish's flavor and digestive benefits.
This recipe utilizes lentils as a plant-forward protein source, contributing to a more sustainable and balanced meal.
Emphasis is placed on using fresh, seasonal herbs and minimizing waste where possible, aligning with eco-conscious cooking principles.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Lamb Loin with Cherry-Orange Glaze and Cheddar Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A clean, white round porcelain plate holds a generous bed of creamy, golden cheddar polenta, its texture smooth and inviting. On top, two or three thick-cut medallions of pan-seared lamb loin are artfully arranged, displaying a beautiful golden-brown crust and a tender, pink interior. A glossy, deep ruby-red cherry-orange glaze is drizzled elegantly over the lamb and around the polenta, adding vibrant color. Fresh green thyme sprigs and finely chopped parsley are scattered sparingly for a fresh aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting, with a silver fork and knife beside the plate and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined, approachable single portion.
instructions: Prepare Cherry-Orange Glaze: In a small saucepan, heat 5 ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced shallots until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute. Add pitted cherries, juice of 1 orange, red wine vinegar, and granulated sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and cherries soften. Mash cherries lightly with a fork. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Cheddar Polenta: In a large saucepan, bring chicken stock to a boil. Slowly whisk in quick-cooking polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring constantly, for 5-7 minutes until polenta is creamy and thick. Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese and 30 g unsalted butter until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Cover to keep warm.

Cook Lamb Loin: Pat lamb loin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 25 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add lamb loin to skillet. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Add 20 g butter and 2 thyme sprigs to skillet. Baste lamb with melted butter. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (140°F) for medium-rare. Remove from oven. Transfer lamb to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest 10 minutes.

Finish and Serve: Slice rested lamb loin into thick medallions. Reheat glaze gently if needed. Spoon a generous portion of creamy cheddar polenta onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 thick lamb medallions on top of the polenta. Drizzle cherry-orange glaze over the lamb and around the plate. Garnish with fresh parsley and remaining thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty roasted chicken and vegetables rests on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, whole roasted chicken thigh with crispy skin is positioned prominently. Around it, thick wedges of roasted potatoes and bright orange, thick-cut carrot rounds are casually arranged, some slightly overlapping. The vegetables exhibit caramelized edges and tender interiors. Fresh green sprigs of rosemary and thyme are scattered for a touch of color and aroma. The dish appears warm and inviting. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A soft, warm light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A casually draped linen napkin is visible in the background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into wedges. Peel carrots. Cut into thick rounds.
Mince garlic cloves. Strip rosemary and thyme leaves from stems. Chop herbs finely.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes and carrots with olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables on the tray.
Cut lemon in half. Squeeze juice over chicken and vegetables. Place lemon halves on the tray.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be crispy and golden. Internal temperature of chicken must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of clear, amber-hued chicken broth is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish in an earthy beige tone. Tender, shredded chicken meat, approximately 2-3 cm chunks, rests gently at the bottom. Vibrant red-orange pieces of fermented kimchi, roughly chopped, are interspersed throughout. The broth is clean and inviting. A delicate sprinkle of golden, crispy chicken skin shards, about 1-2 cm, garnishes the surface, alongside finely minced green cilantro stems. The arrangement is natural and unfussy, highlighting the ingredients' inherent beauty. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed beside it. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, with a clean, minimalist background featuring a hint of blurred green foliage. A simple, elegant ceramic spoon is placed in the bowl.

ingredients.name: Chicken carcass or bone-in chicken pieces (e.g., thighs, drumsticks)
Leftover vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot ends, celery leaves, mushroom stems, garlic skins)

instructions: Place chicken carcass or bone-in chicken pieces and vegetable scraps in a large pot. Add 2 litres of water.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours. Skim any foam.
Remove chicken pieces. When cool enough, remove meat from bones. Shred chicken meat into small chunks. Discard bones and cartilage.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard all solids.
Return strained broth to the pot. Add shredded chicken meat and kimchi.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken meat reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and white pepper. Adjust to taste.
Meanwhile, crisp chicken skin: Place reserved chicken skin in a cold pan. Cook over medium-low heat until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Break into small shards.
Finely mince cilantro or parsley stems.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish with crispy chicken skin shards and minced herb stems. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is free-flowing and spread naturally. Its vibrant orange-red hue contrasts with golden-brown seared chicken chunks, interspersed throughout. Halved, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and texture. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, providing a pale yellow accent. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as garnish, offering a pop of green. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 15 g, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 10 minutes, add halved cherry tomatoes to the risotto. Continue cooking and stirring.
When rice is al dente (creamy but with a slight bite), remove from heat.
Stir in cooked chicken, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter. Stir vigorously for 1 minute for mantecatura (creamy finish).
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring for optimal creaminess.
Ensure broth is hot for continuous cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken & Fermented Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked chicken and pasta is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The plate sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. Large, tender chunks of braised chicken are nestled amongst al dente rigatoni pasta, all coated in a rich, rustic, deep reddish-brown fermented tomato ragu. The sauce has a slightly coarse texture from the slow-cooked vegetables. A few vibrant green basil leaves are scattered artfully on top, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space on the plate. The background is simple and uncluttered, hinting at natural elements like a subtle plant or undyed linen. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the dish, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. A beige, undyed linen napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined restaurant portion.

ingredients.name: Fermented tomato paste or crushed fermented tomatoes
Vegetable scrap stock or chicken stock

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in fermented tomato paste and preserved garlic. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Pour in vegetable scrap stock. Add rosemary sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and easily shreds. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove rosemary sprigs. Shred chicken chunks using two forks directly in the pot, or leave as larger tender pieces.
While chicken simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta cooking water.
Add drained pasta to the chicken ragu. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for a flavorful stock. Consider fermenting your own tomatoes and garlic for deeper, more complex flavors and natural preservation.
Using chicken thighs ensures tender, moist meat after slow cooking. For maximum flavor, use bone-in chicken thighs and remove bones after cooking, or use the bones to make a rich stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken Liver Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Savory Chicken Liver Cake is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its distinct layers. The cake consists of several thin, rich brown liver pancakes, alternating with creamy, pale yellow-white layers of savory filling. The filling reveals finely diced, golden-brown caramelized onions and flecks of vibrant green minced parsley. The texture contrast is evident: smooth, uniform liver layers against the soft, slightly textured filling. The top of the slice is garnished with a sprig of fresh, bright green parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is neat and balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate. In the background, a whole, round Savory Chicken Liver Cake rests on a simple, flat serving platter, lightly garnished with parsley, hinting at its full form. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as an appetizer or main course.
Often accompanied by thinly sliced pickles or fresh tomato slices.
Can be enjoyed with a side of rye bread.
instructions: Rinse chicken liver. Pat dry. Blend liver with eggs, flour, 2.5 g salt, and 2.5 g pepper until smooth. This is your liver batter.

Heat a non-stick pan with a little vegetable oil over medium heat. Pour small amounts of batter to form thin, round pancakes (approximately 15 cm diameter). Cook each pancake for 2-3 minutes per side, until fully cooked through and firm. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Repeat until all batter is used, yielding about 8-10 pancakes. Set aside to cool.
Peel and finely dice onions. Sauté diced onions in remaining vegetable oil until golden and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside to cool.
Peel and mince garlic cloves. Finely chop fresh parsley.
In a bowl, combine sour cream, mayonnaise, minced garlic, chopped parsley, 2.5 g salt, and 2.5 g pepper. Mix well to create the savory filling.

Assemble the cake: Place one liver pancake on a serving plate. Spread a thin, even layer of the sour cream-mayonnaise filling over the pancake. Sprinkle a small amount of sautéed onions over the filling.
Repeat layering with remaining pancakes, filling, and onions. Finish with a top layer of filling. Ensure the sides of the cake are also thinly coated with filling.
Garnish the top of the cake with fresh parsley leaves or finely chopped parsley.
Cover the cake. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow flavors to meld and the cake to set.
notes: While the prompt specified 'sweet' flavor profile, the provided ingredients (chicken liver, onion, garlic, mayonnaise, sour cream) are inherently savory. This recipe has been designed as a traditional savory 'Liver Cake' (Печеночный торт), a popular dish in Eastern European cuisine, which aligns with the ingredient list and 'cake' format.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Rabbit with White Wine and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of braised rabbit is presented on a simple, rustic off-white ceramic plate. The rabbit, in two to three substantial, irregularly shaped chunks, exhibits a rich, deep golden-brown exterior from searing, now tender and glistening from the braising liquid. It is nestled amongst an inviting mix of earthy whole or halved button mushrooms, vibrant orange carrot thick rounds, and soft, roughly chopped onions. A glossy, amber-hued sauce, naturally thickened from the braising, coats the ingredients and pools invitingly at the bottom of the plate. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple fork and knife rest beside the plate, with a casually draped, plain linen napkin nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, emphasizing the comforting, hearty nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette for soaking up the sauce.
A side of simple boiled potatoes or buttered noodles is also traditional.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into thick rounds

instructions: Pat rabbit pieces dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dust rabbit with flour.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add olive oil and butter to the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Sear rabbit pieces in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove rabbit; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return rabbit pieces and cooked bacon to the pot. Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Liquid should mostly cover the rabbit. If not, add more stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until rabbit is very tender and meat easily pulls from the bone.
Add mushrooms to the pot during the last 20 minutes of cooking. Stir gently.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This dish tastes even better the next day. Reheat gently on the stovetop.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Broccoli with Savory Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of roasted chicken and broccoli is presented on a round, rustic off-white ceramic plate, placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. The golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, cut into thick chunks, are nestled against vibrant green broccoli florets. A rich, creamy mustard sauce generously coats the chicken and broccoli, with some pooling at the base. A small mound of fluffy white rice sits beside the main components. The textures are varied: tender chicken, slightly crisp-tender broccoli, and soft rice. The colors are warm and inviting. A simple fork and knife rest beside the plate. The scene is lit with warm, natural kitchen light, conveying a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cook rice according to package directions. Use 200 g rice with 400 ml water. Set aside once cooked.
Cut chicken thighs into thick 3-4 cm chunks. Toss chicken and broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Ensure even coating.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and broccoli is tender-crisp. Stir halfway through.
While chicken roasts, finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and Dijon mustard. Whisk well. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve roasted chicken and broccoli over a bed of cooked rice. Spoon generous amounts of mustard sauce over the chicken and broccoli. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, consider adding a pinch of dried thyme to the roasting chicken and broccoli.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Macaroni with Tomato and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain shallow bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion. Golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh pieces, cooked to tender perfection, are nestled amongst vibrant red macaroni. The macaroni, coated in a rich tomato and oregano sauce, forms a comforting base. A generous scattering of crisp, golden breadcrumbs crowns the dish, providing a delightful textural contrast. Fresh oregano leaves, vibrant green, are sparsely placed for an aromatic and visual pop. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting to highlight the dish's rustic elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Fresh oregano or basil for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir cooked macaroni into the tomato sauce in the pan.
Nestle seared chicken thighs into the macaroni and sauce mixture.
In a small bowl, combine Panko breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese. Sprinkle evenly over the chicken and macaroni.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and breadcrumbs are golden brown and crisp.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh oregano or basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Fermented Butternut Squash Chutney
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial braised chicken thigh, its surface a rich, deep golden-brown, rests centrally on a matte, light-beige ceramic plate. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of rich orange-yellow fermented butternut squash chutney provides a striking color contrast. Scattered over and around the chicken are several irregular, crisp shards of golden-brown chicken skin, adding texture. A light sprinkling of toasted butternut squash seeds is placed artfully for visual interest and a subtle crunch. The plating is minimalist, emphasizing natural forms and allowing ample negative space. The entire dish is bathed in soft, natural light, highlighting the textures and colors of the sustainable ingredients. The setting features a simple reclaimed wood surface and an undyed linen napkin, reinforcing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Butternut Squash Chutney: Peel and dice butternut squash flesh into 1.5 cm cubes. Reserve seeds. Combine diced squash, half of the diced onion, half of the minced garlic, all grated ginger, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, mustard seeds, turmeric, and chili flakes in a clean jar. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, stirring daily, until tangy. Refrigerate.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Carefully remove chicken skin from thighs, keeping it as intact as possible. Set skin aside.

Crisp Chicken Skin: Preheat oven to 180°C. Place chicken skin flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until deeply golden and very crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels. Break into shards.

Sear Chicken: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, flesh-side down, for 3-4 minutes until golden-brown. Flip and sear skin-side down for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Add remaining diced onion and minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened. Deglaze with a splash of chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits.

Braise Chicken: Return chicken thighs to the pan. Pour in remaining chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover the pan tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

Toast Squash Seeds: While chicken braises, clean reserved butternut squash seeds. Toss with a tiny amount of olive oil and salt. Toast in a dry pan over medium heat or bake alongside chicken skin until golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Serve: Remove chicken from oven. Serve each braised chicken thigh with a generous dollop of fermented butternut squash chutney. Garnish with crispy chicken skin shards and toasted butternut squash seeds.
notes: The fermented butternut squash chutney requires 3-5 days of fermentation time, so plan to prepare it in advance.
For a truly zero-waste approach, use chicken bones and trimmings to make your own chicken stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic and Olive Oil Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of spaghetti is loosely coiled and presented on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The pasta strands glisten with olive oil, showing a light coating of sauce. Thinly sliced, pale golden garlic pieces and vibrant red chili flakes are visibly distributed throughout the pasta. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The pasta has a natural, slightly tangled appearance, suggesting a rustic, home-cooked feel. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped beside the plate. A small, rustic ceramic bowl containing grated Parmesan cheese is placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, typical of a home kitchen, with soft shadows enhancing the cozy atmosphere. Traditional Italian flatware, a simple fork, rests beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the flavorful oil.
Enjoy as a simple weeknight meal or a comforting late-night supper.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add generous salt.
Add spaghetti to boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water.
While pasta cooks, thinly slice all garlic cloves.
In a large skillet or pan, heat olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add sliced garlic and red chili flakes to the pan. Cook gently for 3-5 minutes. Garlic should be fragrant and lightly golden, not browned.
Drain the cooked spaghetti. Add directly to the skillet with the garlic oil.
Add 125ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss vigorously to combine and emulsify the sauce.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Add most of the chopped parsley to the pasta. Toss again.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese, if desired.
notes: Ensure garlic does not burn; it should be fragrant and lightly golden to avoid bitterness.
Reserved pasta water is crucial for creating a creamy, emulsified sauce that coats the pasta beautifully.

recipes.recipe_name: Middle Eastern Chicken Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Middle Eastern Chicken Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of golden basmati rice, studded with small diced carrots and soft diced onions, forms the base. Nestled atop the rice are several substantial chunks of seared chicken thigh, each exhibiting a rich, golden-brown crust. The chicken is not sliced. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley leaves provides a fresh counterpoint, alongside a sprinkle of lightly toasted slivered almonds, adding subtle crunch. The presentation is natural and organic, thoughtfully arranged. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, with a white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warm colors and inviting textures. A traditional Middle Eastern-style spoon is placed to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt.
Offer a simple fresh cucumber-tomato salad as an accompaniment.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice until water runs clear. Drain well.
Cut chicken thighs into 4-5cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Work in batches if needed. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrot. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and cinnamon stick. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice to the pot. Stir to coat rice with spices and oil. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Nestle chicken into the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice absorbs liquid and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Do not lift lid.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Remove cinnamon stick.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and toasted slivered almonds.
traditional_techniques: Pilaf cooking method (sautéing aromatics and rice before simmering)

recipes.recipe_name: Pancetta-Wrapped Chicken with Provolone and Turkey Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly golden-brown pancetta-wrapped chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is plump, revealing the slight bulge of its creamy provolone and turkey stuffing. The pancetta is crisped and tightly wrapped, with rendered fat glistening. A rich, light brown pan sauce is spooned artfully beside the chicken, not covering it entirely, allowing its texture and color to show. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast on top of the chicken. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene from the side, casting soft shadows. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound lightly to an even thickness, about 1.5 cm. Season with salt and pepper.
In a bowl, combine ground turkey, diced provolone, chopped spinach, minced garlic, and diced shallot. Mix well.
Divide turkey mixture into four equal portions. Place one portion on one half of each butterflied chicken breast. Fold the other half over the filling.
Carefully wrap each stuffed chicken breast with 2-3 slices of pancetta, ensuring the seam is covered.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear wrapped chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until pancetta is crispy and golden.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth to deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce sauce slightly until it coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken with sauce. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: The turkey in the stuffing adds moisture and a subtle flavor, complementing the chicken without overpowering it.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle al Ragù di Maiale e Olive
recipes.visual_description: The Pappardelle al Ragù di Maiale e Olive is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. Broad pappardelle strands are generously coated in a rich, deep red tomato-based ragu, flecked with dark purple-black olive halves and tender, shredded pieces of browned pork. The pork, having been slow-cooked, retains its rustic, irregular shape. A few vibrant green basil leaves are scattered on top, providing fresh color contrast. A dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmigiano Reggiano adds a final touch. The dish exudes warmth and heartiness. The composition is balanced, showcasing a single refined restaurant portion. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background that suggests a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork shoulder cubes in batches until deeply golden. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half, about 5 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and broth. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Once pork is tender, remove from pot. Shred the pork using two forks. Return shredded pork to the sauce.
Add pitted and halved olives to the ragu. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes to allow flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: The ragu can be made a day in advance; flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: White Bean and Sausage Stew
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of White Bean and Sausage Stew fills a deep, round ceramic bowl. The stew is thick and hearty. Plump, creamy white beans are interspersed with golden-brown, thick-cut sausage rounds. Diced carrots, celery, and onions are visible, softened and coated in the rich, reddish-brown tomato-based broth. A few fresh green parsley leaves are scattered casually on top. The stew has a comforting, slightly irregular texture. The bowl sits on a well-used, light wooden dining table. A simple, slightly off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside it. A few crumbs of crusty bread are scattered nearby. Warm, soft light comes from an overhead kitchen fixture, creating gentle shadows. The background is a slightly blurred, cozy home kitchen scene with minimal, natural clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Drain and rinse white beans. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add whole sausages to the pot. Brown sausages on all sides. This takes about 5-7 minutes.
Remove browned sausages from the pot. Slice them into thick rounds.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Bring the liquid to a simmer.
Return the sliced sausages to the pot. Add the drained white beans.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing the stew to thicken slightly.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Season the stew with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Use good quality pork sausages for best flavor. Cannellini or haricot beans work well.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Onion Compote and Garlic Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table.
