The pan-seared chicken, cooked to a golden-brown exterior and sliced into thick, substantial pieces, is prominently placed. Beside it, a generous mound of apple-onion compote showcases its amber and reddish-brown hues, with visible thinly sliced caramelized onions and small diced apples. Green flecks of fresh thyme are interspersed within the compote. Scattered around the dish are golden, crisp garlic croutons, adding textural contrast. The overall composition is balanced and approachable, characteristic of simple restaurant style. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, contributing to a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, e.g., Honeycrisp or Granny Smith

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
In the same skillet (drain excess oil if necessary), add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Stir in diced apples and minced garlic. Cook 3-5 minutes until apples slightly soften.
Pour in chicken broth and apple cider vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until liquid reduces and compote thickens. Stir in butter and fresh thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
While chicken bakes, cut crusty bread into small cubes. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Toast in a separate pan or bake until golden and crisp.

Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick pieces. Spoon a generous portion of apple-onion compote onto each clean white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange chicken pieces beside the compote. Scatter garlic croutons around the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken and Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The chicken, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is golden-brown with slightly seared edges, scattered naturally across the plate. Alongside are roasted sweet potato wedges, their skins slightly caramelized and interiors soft, displaying warm orange hues. Bright green broccoli florets, some with subtly charred tips, complete the dish, adding a fresh contrast. All components are naturally arranged, touching and overlapping, conveying a comforting, homemade feel. The plate sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. A casually folded, plain linen napkin and a sturdy, everyday stainless steel fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Place in a large bowl.
Peel sweet potatoes. Cut into 2 cm thick wedges. Add to the bowl with chicken.
Cut broccoli into medium florets. Add to the bowl.
Drizzle olive oil over ingredients in the bowl.
Add garlic powder, paprika, dried rosemary, salt, and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients until evenly coated.
Spread mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Do not overcrowd. Use two sheets if needed.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Flip ingredients halfway through roasting.
Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 75°C. Sweet potatoes should be tender.
Remove from oven. Serve immediately.
Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.
notes: This dish is highly versatile. Feel free to substitute other root vegetables like carrots or parsnips, or add bell peppers.
Adjust seasoning to your personal taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Cutlets with San Marzano Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, crispy golden-brown pan-seared chicken cutlet is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. It is generously topped with a vibrant, glistening San Marzano tomato sauce. Draped over the sauce and chicken is melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella cheese, with some areas showing a light golden-brown char from broiling. A few fresh, torn basil leaves are scattered artfully on top, providing a bright green contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the dish's appeal. The setting is a modern bistro style, with a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, accompanied by traditional silver flatware. The lighting is natural, soft, and even, highlighting the dish as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered spaghetti or linguine.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Pair with a crisp green salad tossed in a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally to create two thinner cutlets. Gently pound each cutlet to an even 1.5-2 cm thickness.
Prepare a breading station: Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Combine Panko breadcrumbs, 50g Parmesan, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each chicken cutlet: First coat in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, press into the breadcrumb mixture, ensuring a full, even coating.

Prepare tomato sauce: Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Crush San Marzano tomatoes by hand or with a masher; add to saucepan. Stir in chopped oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Stir in half of the torn basil leaves.
Cook chicken: Heat remaining 45ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully place breaded chicken cutlets in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Pan-sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken to a plate lined with paper towels.
Preheat broiler to high, or oven to 200°C (390°F).
Arrange cooked chicken cutlets on a baking sheet. Spoon a generous amount of tomato sauce over each cutlet. Top with slices or torn pieces of fresh mozzarella.
Broil for 3-5 minutes, or bake for 8-10 minutes, until cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden.
Remove from oven. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and a sprinkle of extra Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for the best sauce flavor.
Ensure chicken cutlets are patted very dry before breading for maximum crispness.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste in both the chicken breading and the tomato sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Dijon Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Dijon Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The risotto, a pale golden hue, forms a fluid, organic mound in the center, its texture visibly creamy with individual al dente rice grains. Scattered throughout are vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets, cut into small, even pieces. Nestled atop the risotto are two to three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions or substantial chunks, showcasing a crisp exterior and juicy interior. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens over the dish. The plate is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and knife and a folded white cotton napkin, under soft, even natural lighting, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chicken to a baking sheet. Finish cooking in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes, then slice into thick medallions or chunks.

In the same frying pan (or a separate pot), melt 20 g butter with remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until fully absorbed.

Add one ladle of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After about 10 minutes of adding stock, stir in the Dijon mustard.

When rice is al dente and risotto is creamy and fluid, remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Fold in the blanched broccoli florets. Check seasoning; add salt and pepper as needed.
Serve risotto immediately. Top each portion with chicken medallions or chunks. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure risotto remains fluid and creamy, not dry. Add more stock if needed.
Always check chicken internal temperature to ensure it reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Macaroni with Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Macaroni with Seared Chicken is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The macaroni, cooked al dente, is coated in a rich, creamy, orange-red tomato sauce, flecked with fine diced onion and minced garlic. Irregularly shaped, golden-brown seared chicken chunks (approximately 3-4 cm) are nestled throughout the pasta. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, coarsely chopped fresh basil leaves garnishes the top, along with a dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The dish exhibits a glossy sheen from the sauce. The bowl sits on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish. The background is simple and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to soak up the creamy sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook, stirring, until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Stir in dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Add dry macaroni to the simmering sauce. Stir well. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes, or until macaroni is al dente. Add more chicken broth if the sauce becomes too thick.

Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Stir in heavy cream and shredded mozzarella cheese. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until cheese is melted and sauce is creamy. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Taste the dish. Adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle the creamy tomato macaroni and chicken onto individual serving plates. Garnish with fresh chopped basil or parsley and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Adjust the amount of chicken broth to achieve desired sauce consistency; the macaroni will absorb liquid as it cooks.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Marinara and Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly portioned Chicken Parmesan is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of al dente penne pasta, lightly coated in rich red marinara sauce, forms the base. Centered on the pasta is a whole, golden-brown breaded chicken breast, generously topped with melted, bubbly, and slightly browned fresh mozzarella. A vibrant red marinara sauce pools around the chicken, with some sauce clinging to the penne. Fresh green basil leaves, some torn, some whole, are scattered artfully over the cheese and around the plate, providing a fresh contrast. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a final touch. The dish is set on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a clean white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware placed neatly beside the plate. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is a gently blurred, warm-toned modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the marinara sauce.
instructions: Prepare chicken breasts. Pound each to 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up dredging station: Plate 1 with flour, Plate 2 with beaten eggs, Plate 3 with breadcrumbs.
Dredge chicken: Coat each breast in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Press crumbs to adhere.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Pan-fry chicken: Cook 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Prepare marinara sauce: In the same pan, add remaining 30ml olive oil. Sauté minced garlic 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta: Boil penne according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Assemble: Place pan-fried chicken breasts into the simmering marinara sauce. Top each chicken breast with mozzarella slices.
Bake: Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 10-12 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Serve: Place a portion of penne on each plate. Top with a chicken Parmesan breast and extra marinara sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan.
notes: Pound chicken breasts to an even thickness for uniform cooking and a more tender texture.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Persimmon & Black Currant Galette
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, rustic whole wheat galette slice with visible caramelized persimmon and shallots forms the base. Several succulent, thick chunks of pan-seared duck breast, displaying crispy, deeply rendered skin and a tender, rosy interior, are artfully placed on top of or beside the galette. A glossy, deep ruby-red black currant and raisin reduction sauce is elegantly drizzled over the duck and creates a rich pool around the dish. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the duck, providing a subtle color contrast. The entire plate is visible, showcasing moderate negative space and a balanced composition. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with a neatly folded dark grey cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a softly blurred, casual restaurant-style background.

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (e.g., Merlot or Pinot Noir)

instructions: Prepare galette dough: In a large bowl, combine whole wheat flour and a pinch of salt. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add ice water, mixing until dough forms. Do not overmix. Flatten into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

Prepare galette filling: Peel and dice persimmons into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice shallots. In a pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté shallots until softened, about 3 minutes. Add diced persimmons and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble galette: On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough into a 30 cm circle. Transfer to the prepared baking tray. Spread the persimmon-shallot mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 4 cm border. Fold the dough border over the filling, crimping slightly. Brush the exposed crust with egg yolk wash.
Bake galette for 25-30 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and filling is tender. Remove from oven and let rest.

Prepare black currant reduction: In a small saucepan, combine black currants, raisins, red wine, duck stock, and honey/maple syrup. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract liquid. Discard solids. Keep sauce warm.

Cook duck breast: Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes, until skin is crispy and golden brown. Pour off excess fat. Flip duck breasts and sear meat-side down for 3 minutes.

Finish duck breast: Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let duck breasts rest for 5 minutes before slicing into thick chunks or medallions.

To plate: Place a slice of the persimmon galette on each plate. Arrange several thick chunks of rested duck breast on top or beside the galette. Spoon the warm black currant reduction generously over the duck and around the plate. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Piccata with Linguine
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single portion of glossy linguine pasta swirled into a nest in the center of a clean white porcelain plate. A whole, golden-brown seared chicken breast sits atop the pasta, coated in a shimmering lemon-butter sauce. The sauce is speckled with small, dark green capers and finely chopped bright green parsley. The chicken shows a crisp, flour-dredged texture with deep amber caramelization. Beside the plate lies a polished silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak bistro table. A small wedge of fresh lemon is placed on the side. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the silky texture of the emulsified sauce and the vibrant herbs.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a warmed porcelain plate
Accompany with crusty focaccia bread
Provide extra lemon wedges on the side
instructions: Boil salted water.
Cook linguine until al dente.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken in flour.
Shake off excess flour.
Heat oil and 20g butter in a large skillet.
Sear chicken until golden brown.
Verify internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet.
Add stock, lemon juice, and capers to the pan.
Scrape pan bottom to deglaze.
Reduce liquid by half over high heat.
Whisk in remaining butter to emulsify.
Toss pasta and parsley in the sauce.
Place pasta on plates.
Top with the whole chicken breast.
notes: Ensure the sauce is fully emulsified before adding pasta
Maintain a fluid sauce consistency to coat the linguine evenly

recipes.recipe_name: Georgian Beef and Potato Skillet (Ojakhuri)
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Georgian Beef and Potato Skillet (Ojakhuri) is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Thick, irregular chunks of seared beef, rich brown with tender interiors, are nestled among golden-brown potato wedges. Translucent, caramelized onion slices are interspersed throughout. Bright green peas add pops of color. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped mint leaves provides a fragrant contrast. The dish has a natural, slightly rustic sheen from the pan juices. The plate rests on a well-worn, dark wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside it. A piece of traditional Georgian puri (flatbread) is visible on the table. Soft, warm kitchen light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh Georgian bread (puri) for dipping.
Accompanied by a simple fresh tomato and cucumber salad.
instructions: Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 3-4 cm wedges or large chunks.
Thinly slice onions. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add beef chunks to the hot skillet. Sear until browned on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Remove beef and set aside.
Add potato wedges to the same skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden-brown and slightly tender, about 10-12 minutes. Remove potatoes and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the skillet. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared beef and potatoes to the skillet with the onions and garlic.
Stir well to combine. Add 100 ml water or beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in green peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Remove from heat.
Roughly chop fresh mint. Garnish the dish generously with chopped mint before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality beef chuck that benefits from slow simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, cut into 2-3 thick, irregular chunks, rests atop a vibrant, smooth pool of deep red fermented tomato puree. Surrounding the chicken, 3-4 golden-orange roasted carrot batons are artfully scattered, their edges slightly caramelized. A scattering of delicate, golden-brown crispy onion skins adds height and textural contrast. A small sprig of fresh thyme sits beside the chicken. The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte, cream-colored ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, organic rim. The plate is centered on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table surface. To the side, an undyed, crumpled linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of soft green from a blurred plant, emphasizing an eco-conscious setting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single, refined restaurant portion with ample negative space. Ingredients are arranged naturally, avoiding geometric shapes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as the centerpiece of a mindful, seasonal meal.
Accompany with simple, locally sourced greens.
Embrace the philosophy of consuming mindfully and reducing waste.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Puree: Wash and quarter tomatoes. Place in a clean, airtight jar. Add 10 g sea salt. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp jar daily. Once fermented, blend tomatoes into a smooth puree. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Roasted Carrots: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and peel carrots. Cut into thick batons (approx. 5 cm long). Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender-crisp and caramelized. Set aside.

Prepare Crispy Onion Skins: Carefully peel outer, dry layers from onions. Wash skins thoroughly. Pat completely dry with a clean towel. Heat 125 ml neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Fry onion skins in batches until golden brown and crispy. This takes 1-2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season immediately with a pinch of sea salt. Set aside.

Prepare Pan-Seared Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 45 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Cut each thigh into 2-3 thick, irregular chunks.

Assemble the Dish: Spoon a generous pool of fermented tomato puree onto the center of each plate. Arrange chicken chunks on top of the puree. Artfully scatter roasted carrot batons around the chicken. Garnish with crispy onion skins and a fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: Fermenting tomatoes enhances their flavor and adds beneficial probiotics.
Using onion skins is a zero-waste technique that adds a unique, savory crispness.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and room temperature.
The remaining onion can be diced and used in other recipes, or thinly sliced and pickled.

recipes.recipe_name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in poached chicken with glossy, pale skin. The chicken rests on a bed of fragrant, light-yellow Jasmine rice infused with ginger and pandan. Slices of fresh, cool cucumber are arranged neatly to the side. The chicken is lightly drizzled with a mixture of soy sauce and sesame oil. Three small ceramic dipping bowls contain bright red chili sauce, dark soy sauce, and a vibrant green ginger-scallion oil. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate on a light wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a traditional ceramic soup spoon sit to the right. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side bowl of hot chicken broth
Include chili sauce, ginger-garlic sauce, and dark soy sauce
Serve at room temperature as per tradition
instructions: Rub chicken with salt to remove impurities.
Rinse chicken under cold water.
Boil 3 liters of water with 30g crushed ginger and scallions.
Submerge chicken in boiling water.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and cover pot.
Steep chicken for 30 minutes.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Submerge chicken in ice water for 5 minutes.
Drain chicken and rub skin with sesame oil.
Sauté 20g minced ginger and minced garlic in chicken fat.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add 600ml poaching liquid and pandan leaves.
Cook rice until liquid is absorbed.
Cut chicken into large chunks.
notes: Save the remaining poaching liquid for a light soup
Rubbing the chicken with salt ensures a smooth skin texture
Using rendered chicken fat for the rice is essential for authenticity

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Liver & Sweet Onion Terrine Cake
recipes.visual_description: A precise 2cm thick slice of Chicken Liver & Sweet Onion Terrine Cake rests elegantly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The terrine displays distinct layers: a smooth, rich, light brown chicken liver base contrasting with pockets of deeper orange, caramelized onion and carrot. Its texture appears firm and creamy. A small, vibrant spoonful of the reserved, glistening sweet onion and carrot compote is artfully placed beside the terrine slice, adding a pop of warm orange. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the terrine, providing a touch of green. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted crusty baguette slices or brioche.
Offer small cornichons (gherkins) or pickled onions on the side for acidity.
A light, crisp green salad with a simple vinaigrette complements the richness.
instructions: Heat butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and carrot. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes until very soft and deeply caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add sugar and balsamic vinegar; cook 2 minutes more. Set aside 1/3 of the caramelized mixture for compote.
Briefly sear cleaned chicken livers in the same skillet for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Do not fully cook through.

Combine remaining caramelized onion-carrot mixture, seared chicken livers, egg, sour cream, mayonnaise, minced garlic, flour, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper in a food processor. Process until smooth.
Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a 1-liter terrine mold or loaf pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides.
Pour the liver mixture into the prepared mold. Smooth the top.
Place the terrine mold in a larger roasting pan. Fill the roasting pan with hot water to come halfway up the sides of the terrine mold (bain-marie).
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). A skewer inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove terrine from oven. Let cool slightly in the water bath. Remove from water bath.
Place a weight (e.g., a foil-wrapped brick or cans) on top of the terrine while it cools to compress it. Refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until firm.
To serve, gently lift the terrine from the mold using the parchment paper. Slice into 2cm thick pieces.
Reheat the reserved caramelized onion and carrot mixture gently. Serve alongside the terrine slices as a sweet compote.
notes: Chilling the terrine thoroughly is crucial for a firm texture and clean slices.
Ensure chicken liver reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Corn Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, generous individual portion of Spicy Chicken & Corn Skillet is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally mounded with ample negative space. Golden-brown, seared chicken cubes are mixed with brightly colored vegetables. Red and yellow bell peppers are cut into 1 cm strips, softened yet retaining form. One cm diced red onion, bright yellow corn kernels, and diced red tomatoes add pops of color and juicy texture. The dish is garnished with fresh, roughly chopped green cilantro. A lime wedge rests beside the mound. The plating is clean, professional, and approachable. The dish is accompanied by warm corn tortillas and a small ramekin of vibrant red tomato salsa, placed on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of lime wedges for extra zest.
Serve with traditional tomato salsa or pico de gallo.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt, pepper, chili powder, and cumin.
Dice onion into 1 cm pieces. Slice bell peppers into 1 cm strips. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add seasoned chicken. Sear chicken until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion and bell pepper strips to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add corn kernels and diced tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add hot sauce, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Stir well to combine. Cook for 5 minutes, ensuring chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from heat. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the mixture. Stir in chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately with warm corn tortillas and salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy chicken and broccoli is presented in a clean, white, shallow bowl. Thick, irregular chunks of pan-seared chicken, boasting a golden-brown crust, are nestled among vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. All elements are generously coated in a rich, pale yellow cheddar sauce, flecked with bright red chili and green herbs. The sauce has a smooth, appealing texture. A light sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or chives and a thin slice of red chili adorn the top, adding freshness and color. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and modern flatware beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and half of the smoked paprika.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and finely minced chili. Sauté until onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and remaining smoked paprika. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the onion mixture. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer.
Add broccoli florets. Cover skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Stir in heavy cream and grated cheddar cheese. Cook, stirring, until cheese is melted and sauce is creamy and thickened. Do not boil vigorously once cream is added.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Stir to coat chicken with sauce. Heat through for 1-2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Potato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single refined portion of Roasted Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Potato Pasta is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy, off-white tone. A modest, organic mound of short pasta, tossed with a rich, rustic red fermented tomato sauce and small, golden-brown roasted potato cubes, occupies one side of the plate. The sauce clings naturally to the pasta and potatoes, showcasing their inherent textures. Beside the pasta, a single roasted chicken thigh, skin deeply golden and visibly crispy, rests as a whole piece. A few thin, translucent rings of pickled red onion are scattered artfully over the pasta, adding a subtle pop of color. A sprig of fresh green parsley or a few basil leaves provides a natural, unfussy garnish. The composition emphasizes natural spacing and avoids overcrowding, allowing the ceramic plate's surface to provide ample white space. The table surface is a light-colored reclaimed wood, revealing its natural grain. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the textures and colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural plant greenery visible, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato sauce: Wash tomatoes. Roughly chop. Place in a clean jar. Add 10g sea salt per 500g tomatoes. Cover with water. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached. Blend fermented tomatoes into a smooth sauce when ready to use.

Prepare pickled onion: Thinly slice half of the brown onion. Place in a small jar. Cover with equal parts hot water and white vinegar. Add a pinch of salt and sugar. Seal. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and crispy. Reserve potato skins for crispy garnish if desired.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, cook pasta according to package directions in salted water. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

In a large pan, sauté minced garlic and remaining half of the onion (diced) in a little olive oil until softened. Add the fermented tomato sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir in cooked pasta and roasted potato cubes. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency. Toss to combine.
Plate pasta mixture. Place one roasted chicken thigh beside the pasta. Garnish with pickled onion rings and fresh parsley or basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek with Fondant Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of braised beef cheek rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, a rich, dark brown, is presented as a whole, tender chunk, showing its fall-apart texture. Beside it, two to three golden-brown fondant potato cylinders stand neatly, revealing their crispy seared exterior. A vibrant, smooth butternut squash puree is artfully swirled or spooned onto the plate, offering a contrasting orange hue. A few glistening, soft confit cherry tomato halves are scattered, adding pops of red and a touch of sweetness. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Season beef cheeks with salt and pepper. Render 30g beef fat in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.

Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add 4 minced garlic cloves; cook 1 minute. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.

Return beef cheeks to the pot. Add 750ml beef stock, 2 sprigs thyme, 2 sprigs rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

Peel potatoes. Cut into thick cylinders, about 5 cm tall and 4 cm diameter. Melt 20g beef fat in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear potato cylinders on one flat side until deeply golden-brown. Flip.

Add 200 ml beef stock, 1 sprig thyme, and 20g butter to the potato skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cover. Transfer to oven with beef cheeks for the last 40-50 minutes, or until tender and liquid has reduced. Baste occasionally.

Peel, deseed, and cut butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Dice half an onion. Sauté diced onion in 10g butter until translucent. Add squash cubes and 100 ml beef stock. Simmer until squash is very tender. Blend until smooth, adding more stock or butter if needed. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 130°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Arrange in a small oven-safe dish. Add 2 minced garlic cloves, remaining 20ml olive oil, and 1 sprig thyme. Season lightly with salt. Roast for 45-60 minutes, until softened and slightly shriveled but still plump.

Remove beef cheeks from braising liquid. Strain braising liquid, pressing on solids. Skim excess fat. Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until it reaches a sauce consistency. Adjust seasoning.

To plate, place a spoonful of butternut squash puree on each plate. Arrange one braised beef cheek beside the puree. Place 2-3 golden-brown fondant potato cylinders neatly beside the beef. Scatter a few glistening confit tomatoes around the dish. Spoon rich braising sauce over the beef. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy roasted butternut squash soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, warm golden-orange hue. The soup's surface is smooth and inviting, with a thin swirl of cream visible if added. A light scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley serves as the sole, functional garnish, adding a touch of freshness. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, reflecting a homely family kitchen setting. Natural, soft lighting from a nearby window or kitchen fixture illuminates the scene. A simple, slightly textured cloth napkin is casually draped beside the bowl, with a plain metal spoon resting next to it. The arrangement is natural and unforced, emphasizing comfort and warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve butternut squash. Scoop out seeds. Peel skin. Cut squash into 3 cm cubes.
Peel and quarter onion. Peel garlic cloves.
Toss squash cubes, quartered onion, and garlic cloves with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a large pot. Add vegetable broth.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to purée soup until completely smooth.
Stir in heavy cream and nutmeg.
Return to low heat. Warm through without boiling.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Forest Mushroom and Potato Gratin with Savory Tomato Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined individual portion of Forest Mushroom and Potato Gratin is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin is presented as a thick, rectangular slice, showcasing distinct, tender layers of thinly sliced, golden-brown potatoes and savory, earthy mushrooms. The top layer of the gratin is beautifully golden and slightly crisp, with visible hints of browned potato edges. A rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown savory tomato reduction is artfully pooled around the base of the gratin, creating a vibrant contrast. The sauce is smooth and inviting. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are delicately placed atop the gratin and scattered around the sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. A light scattering of golden-brown, toasted breadcrumbs adds a textural element over the sauce. The plating is organized and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) positioned appropriately. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting ambiance with a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm gratin dish.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes using a mandoline. Arrange a single layer of potato slices in the prepared gratin dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Clean and roughly chop mushrooms. Peel and finely dice shallots and garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chopped mushrooms and sauté until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter. Add diced shallots and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add 1 minced garlic clove and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Layer half of the sautéed mushrooms over the potatoes in the gratin dish. Scatter a few fresh basil leaves. Repeat with another layer of thinly sliced potatoes, seasoned. Top with remaining mushrooms and basil.
Pour 200 ml vegetable stock evenly over the gratin. Cover tightly with foil. Bake for 40 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.

While gratin bakes, prepare the sauce. Halve or quarter plum tomatoes. Dice pineapple into small cubes. In a small saucepan, combine diced pineapple, raspberries, and granulated sugar. Cook over medium heat until fruit softens and releases juices, about 5 minutes.

Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and red wine vinegar to the fruit mixture. Cook for 2 minutes until vinegar reduces slightly. Add roasted tomatoes, remaining 300 ml vegetable stock, and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in dark chocolate until melted and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and black pepper.
Carefully transfer sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined consistency. Keep warm.

For breadcrumbs, pulse stale rustic bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Toast breadcrumbs in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden brown and crispy, about 5 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt.
Remove gratin from oven. Increase oven temperature to 200°C. Remove foil and bake for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and crispy.

To serve, cut the gratin into 4 generous squares or rectangles. Place one portion on each plate. Spoon a generous pool of the warm tomato reduction around the gratin. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and a sprinkle of toasted breadcrumbs for crunch. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Ginger Sorbet with Candied Apple Peel
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Apple & Ginger Sorbet is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl. A single, generous scoop of the pale golden-green sorbet sits elegantly, its smooth yet subtly textured surface indicating its refreshing, icy nature. Its natural color highlights the fresh apples and ginger. A few delicate, translucent candied apple peels are scattered gently on top, their edges slightly curled, adding a crisp, contrasting texture. The minimalistic plating leaves ample negative space within the bowl. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, its visible grain providing an organic foundation. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the textures and natural colors for a clean, inviting, and eco-conscious presentation.
instructions: Wash apples. Peel apples and reserve peels. Core apples and chop flesh into small cubes.
Combine chopped apple with grated ginger and a pinch of salt in a non-reactive bowl. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature (20-22°C) for 24-48 hours. Stir once or twice.
Transfer apple-ginger mixture to a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth over a bowl. Press firmly to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Stir maple syrup and lemon juice into the fermented apple-ginger liquid. Chill mixture thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
While sorbet base chills, combine reserved apple peels with 100 ml water and 50 g sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 10-15 minutes until peels are tender.
Drain peels and spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 100°C for 30-45 minutes, or until crisp. Let cool.
Pour the chilled sorbet base into an ice cream maker. Churn according to manufacturer's instructions until soft-serve consistency.
Transfer sorbet to a freezer-safe container. Freeze for at least 2-4 hours to firm up.
Scoop sorbet into chilled bowls. Garnish with crisp candied apple peels.
notes: For a deeper fermented flavor, allow the apple-ginger mixture to ferment for up to 72 hours, tasting periodically.
Ensure apples are ripe for best flavor.
Adjust maple syrup quantity based on apple sweetness and personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spicy Sausage, Crispy Pancetta, and Smoked Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Rigatoni with Spicy Sausage, Crispy Pancetta, and Smoked Mozzarella is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente rigatoni is coated in a rustic, vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with golden-brown, crumbled Italian sausage. Melted, stringy smoked mozzarella is visible throughout the pasta, creating a rich texture. Scattered generously over the top are small, crisp, dark brown diced pancetta pieces, providing a textural contrast. Bright green, freshly chopped basil leaves are sprinkled over the dish for color and aroma. The pasta is piled naturally in the center, allowing moderate negative space on the plate's white rim. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware positioned beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for pasta.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy.
Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat in the pan.
Add sausage meat to the same pan. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through.
Drain excess fat if needed. Remove sausage from pan.
Add olive oil to the pan if needed. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Let sauce simmer gently for 15-20 minutes.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120ml of pasta water.
Add cooked sausage and half of the smoked mozzarella to the tomato sauce. Stir to combine.
Add drained rigatoni to the sauce. Add Pecorino Romano and half of the reserved pasta water. Toss well to coat pasta.
Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with remaining smoked mozzarella, crispy pancetta, and fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sweetbreads and Shrimp with Asadero Potato Purée and Pastis-Maggi Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a simple light wooden table. A smooth, creamy mound of pale yellow Asadero potato purée forms the base. Golden-brown seared sweetbread chunks, about 3-4 cm, are arranged artfully on one side of the purée, showcasing their crisp exterior. Adjacent, plump, pinkish-orange seared shrimp are neatly placed. A scattering of deep red kidney beans adds contrast around the protein. A glistening, amber-hued Pastis-Maggi jus is artfully drizzled over the sweetbreads and shrimp. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh pop of color. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the textures and colors of the ingredients. A simple folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating a professional and inviting atmosphere with a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Prepare sweetbreads: Soak in cold water 30 minutes. Drain. Blanch in boiling salted water 5 minutes. Plunge into ice bath. Remove membrane and sinew. Press between plates with weight for 30 minutes. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry. Dredge lightly in flour.

Prepare potato purée: Peel and cube potatoes. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Return to pot. Add 40g butter, cream, and shredded Asadero cheese. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Pastis-Maggi Jus: Dice shallots. Mince garlic. Heat 10ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Sauté shallots until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute more. Deglaze with Pastis. Cook until nearly evaporated. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half. Stir in Maggi seasoning. Swirl in remaining 20g butter until melted and emulsified. Season to taste. Keep warm.

Sear sweetbreads: Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add sweetbreads. Sear until golden brown and crisp on all sides, about 4-5 minutes total. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from pan. Keep warm.
Sear shrimp: Add shrimp to the same pan. Sear 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm kidney beans: Rinse kidney beans. Gently warm in a small saucepan or microwave.

Plate the dish: Spoon a generous portion of Asadero potato purée onto each plate. Arrange seared sweetbread chunks and shrimp on top of the purée. Scatter warm kidney beans around the plate. Drizzle Pastis-Maggi Jus over the sweetbreads and shrimp. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Potato-Onion Hash and Melted Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared beef medallion, perfectly medium-rare with a rich brown crust, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick slice of creamy, slightly melted mozzarella drapes over the beef. Adjacent to the medallion, a neat, rustic mound of golden-brown potato-onion hash, featuring crisp-edged potato cubes and softened, translucent onion pieces, creates a textural contrast. Bright green, fresh basil leaves are scattered artfully over the beef and hash, adding a vibrant color pop and herbaceous aroma. A subtle sheen of pan sauce glazes the beef and parts of the hash. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well.
Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add finely diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add cooked potato cubes to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are lightly browned and slightly crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a separate heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Place a slice of mozzarella on top of each medallion. Cover loosely with foil to melt cheese slightly while resting, about 5 minutes.
Optional pan sauce: Deglaze the beef pan with red wine (if using) and beef stock. Scrape up browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced, about 2-3 minutes.

Plate: Place a generous mound of potato-onion hash on one side of each plate. Arrange a beef medallion with melted mozzarella next to the hash. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken and Vegetable Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Chicken and Vegetable Noodle Soup is presented in a clean, off-white porcelain bowl, centered on a rustic wooden table. The rich, amber-colored broth fills the bowl, with tender, diced chicken chunks, soft diced potatoes, vibrant orange diced carrots, and red diced bell peppers visible throughout. Medium-width egg noodles are nestled among the ingredients. The soup is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The arrangement is natural and inviting, showcasing the textures and colors of the ingredients. A simple, folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. The lighting is natural and even, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere without harsh shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting, allowing the soup to remain the clear focal point.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and diced (e.g., Yukon Gold)

instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm pieces. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear until lightly browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer, uncovered, for 15 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in egg noodles. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or according to package directions, until noodles are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork Ragu with Pappardelle and Bel Paese
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Pork Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The broad pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark red ragu, with visible tender shredded pork chunks. The dish is garnished with vibrant green, freshly torn basil leaves scattered naturally over the ragu and a few delicate, pale yellow dollops of melted Bel Paese cheese. The plating is clean and professional, allowing for moderate negative space around the well-proportioned elements. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with deep reds, pale yellows, and fresh green accents. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white porcelain dinner plate serves as a base. A silver fork is placed beside the bowl. A clean, folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background that remains unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the ragu.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat pork shoulder dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic and Calabrian chili paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and bay leaves. Add chicken stock if needed to just cover the pork.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove pork from the pot. Shred pork using two forks. Discard any excess fat or gristle. Return shredded pork to the ragu. Stir well. Remove bay leaves.
Taste ragu and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in deep bowls. Top each serving with small dollops or thin slices of Bel Paese cheese and fresh torn basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, round, white ceramic plate. A modest individual portion of One-Pot Chicken and Tomato Rice fills the center. The rice is a warm, orange-red, with individual grains and soft diced onion visible. A whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh rests on the rice, nestled slightly. The chicken is tender. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the chicken and rice. The setting is a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene. A simple, folded linen napkin is casually placed next to the plate. Basic fork and knife are laid out. The background shows hints of a homely kitchen, conveying comforting, expertly prepared home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes (undrained) and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Check chicken for doneness (75°C).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Mediterranean Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, placed centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. Around it, a cluster of tender, golden-roasted potato chunks, some with visible herb flecks and softened garlic cloves. A few bright red roasted cherry tomatoes provide pops of color. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprig of rosemary and a small lemon wedge. Colors are rich golden-brown chicken skin, rustic golden potatoes, vibrant red tomatoes, deep green rosemary, and bright yellow lemon. Textures include crispy chicken skin, tender chicken meat, and fluffy interior of potatoes with slightly crisp exteriors. Served on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights textures. A traditional, simple metal fork and knife are placed to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up pan juices.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (small, like new potatoes, or Yukon Gold, quartered)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into uniform 3cm chunks.
Peel and smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, garlic, rosemary, thyme, and olive oil. Toss well to coat.
Nestle chicken thighs among potatoes in the pan. Add cherry tomatoes.
Slice half a lemon into thin rounds. Tuck lemon rounds into the pan.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Pour chicken broth into the pan.
Continue roasting for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Skin should be golden brown and crisp. Potatoes should be tender.
Squeeze juice from the remaining half lemon over the chicken and potatoes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
For extra crisp skin, pat chicken very dry before seasoning.
traditional_techniques: Using fresh herbs and citrus to brighten flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef and Potato Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic white porcelain bowl, showcasing a rich, vibrant mahogany-red stew. Large, succulent chunks of slow-braised beef are nestled alongside uniform cubes of tender, golden-yellow potatoes. The sauce is glossy and thick, clinging to the ingredients. A single dollop of thick sour cream and a sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley garnish the center. The bowl sits on a dark wooden bistro table next to a thick slice of crusty sourdough bread. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and the coarse texture of the braised meat. A vintage pewter spoon rests on a folded white linen napkin beside the plate, creating an authentic Hungarian dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of csipetke (hand-pinched noodles)
Accompany with fermented pickles or a cucumber salad
Provide extra sour cream (tejföl) on the table

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

instructions: Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef cubes and return to heat.
Sear beef for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell peppers.
Pour in beef stock to cover the meat.
Simmer covered on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potato cubes to the pot.
Cook for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Do not burn the paprika or it will turn bitter.
Use high-quality Hungarian paprika for the most authentic color and flavor.
Ensure the beef is cut into uniform chunks for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Braised Chicken with Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken, with its golden-brown, slightly crispy skin, is nestled within a rich, rustic tomato sauce. The sauce features visible, softened chunks of red tomato and translucent pieces of roughly chopped onion, creating a hearty, comforting texture. A few vibrant green, torn basil leaves are scattered naturally over the chicken and sauce. The plate sits on a well-worn, dark wood kitchen table, showing slight imperfections. A casually folded, plain linen napkin and a torn piece of crusty bread are placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by soft, warm, natural light, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The presentation is unpretentious, focusing on the wholesome appeal of home-cooked comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add sliced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Add dried oregano. Bring mixture to a simmer.

Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in fresh basil just before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
This dish reheats well and flavors deepen overnight.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (for sautéing onion and garlic base)

recipes.recipe_name: Uzbek-Style Beef and Carrot Plov
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Uzbek-Style Beef and Carrot Plov is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. The plov is mounded, showcasing its layered composition. Tender, golden-brown beef chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are visible throughout. Vibrant orange carrot matchsticks, softened and slightly caramelized, are interspersed with fluffy, distinct grains of long-grain rice, pearled barley, and brown lentils. The overall color palette is warm, with rich browns, oranges, and the off-white of the grains. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro or dill adorns the top for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. A polished metal spoon or fork rests beside the plate. A small, simple white bowl containing a few slices of tomato and red onion (Achichuk salad) sits adjacent to the main plate, offering a traditional accompaniment. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Prepare ingredients: Rinse rice, barley, and lentils separately until water runs clear. Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Slice onions thinly. Cut carrots into thick matchsticks (julienne).
Heat oil: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat oil over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef: Add beef chunks. Sear until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Sauté onions: Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté until deeply caramelized and golden brown. This takes 10-15 minutes.
Add carrots and spices: Add carrots and whole cumin seeds. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until carrots soften slightly. Add crushed coriander seeds, salt, and pepper.

Build zirvak: Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes. Add enough hot water or stock to just cover the ingredients (about 600 ml). Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Place the whole garlic head (top sliced off) in the center. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes. This forms the 'zirvak'.
Add grains: Carefully layer the rinsed barley evenly over the zirvak. Then layer the rinsed lentils. Finally, layer the rinsed rice evenly over the top. Do not stir the layers.
Add more liquid: Gently pour additional hot water or stock over a spoon onto the rice until it is about 1-2 cm above the rice level (approx. 200 ml, adjust as needed).
Cook plov: Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Cook for 25-30 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and grains are tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.

Rest and serve: Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10-15 minutes. Gently fluff and mix the plov before serving. Discard the garlic head or serve the cloves. Garnish with fresh cilantro or dill. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Mushroom Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork and Mushroom Rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow, white porcelain pasta bowl, centered on a simple light wooden table. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, dark red tomato-based ragu, with tender, irregular chunks of braised pork and soft, sliced cremini mushrooms visible throughout. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, adding a pop of color. A dusting of grated Pecorino Romano cheese lightly coats the surface. Textures include al dente pasta, succulent pork, and a thick, savory sauce. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors. The background is clean, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Offer additional grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 2-3 cm chunks. Season pork with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 3 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While ragu simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water.
Stir chopped fresh basil into the ragu. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water if sauce is too thick.
Serve hot in individual pasta bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Chicken, Rice, and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the One-Pot Chicken, Rice, and Broccoli is presented on a round, rustic off-white ceramic plate. The dish forms a natural mound in the center, with cooked rice, tender chicken chunks, and vibrant green broccoli florets visibly integrated. The components are casually arranged, touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a comforting, homemade feel. Chicken is cut into substantial 3cm chunks, browned from searing. Onion is diced and integrated into the rice. Garlic is minced. Broccoli is cut into small, bite-sized florets, still holding their shape with a slight tender-crisp texture. The rice is soft and fluffy, with a light golden hue. Chicken chunks display a golden-brown exterior. Broccoli florets maintain their bright green color. A sprinkle of freshly chopped parsley adds a touch of contrasting green. The plate rests on a well-used, slightly distressed wooden dining table. A simple, dark blue checkered cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. A sturdy, silver fork with a slightly worn finish is placed on the napkin. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft natural light, suggesting a cozy kitchen or dining area during a family meal. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere without distraction.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Season with half the salt and pepper. Sear chicken until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed rice. Cook for 1 minute, coating grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Add remaining salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.

Distribute broccoli florets over the rice and chicken. Cover and cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, and broccoli is tender-crisp. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Beef Medallions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef and pork medallions arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef medallions are thick-cut, cooked to a medium-rare, displaying a rich brown crust. The pork medallions are similarly thick-cut, seared to a golden-brown with a tender interior. A generous mound of golden-brown caramelized onion thin slices is placed beside the meats. A vibrant, glossy hot mustard glaze is drizzled artfully over the medallions and around the plate. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread
Serve with roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat beef and pork medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Sear beef medallions 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and golden brown.
Add minced garlic to onions. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in beef broth, Dijon mustard, hot sauce, brown sugar, and cayenne pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring, until glaze slightly thickens.
Return beef and pork medallions to skillet with glaze. Turn to coat meat. Heat through 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Turkey Medallions with Creamy Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Turkey Medallions with Creamy Garlic Sauce is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three golden-brown seared turkey medallions, appearing as whole pieces, are centrally placed. A rich, off-white creamy garlic sauce is generously spooned over and around the turkey, showcasing its smooth texture. To the side, roasted baby potatoes, halved with golden-crisp skins, are artfully arranged. A neat cluster of vibrant green, tender-crisp blanched green beans completes the main components. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkling of fresh, bright green chopped parsley over the turkey and sauce, and a small, bright yellow lemon wedge rests near the plate's edge. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by polished silverware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish against a softly blurred, casual restaurant-style background, emphasizing the food as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Offer crusty bread for dipping into the creamy sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and halve or quarter baby potatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Trim turkey breast. Slice turkey into 1.5 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove turkey from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 15 g butter to the same pan. Sauté diced shallot for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3 minutes.
Stir in double cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Season sauce with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
Return turkey medallions to the pan with the sauce. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to heat through.
While sauce simmers, blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well.
Serve turkey medallions with creamy garlic sauce. Arrange roasted potatoes and blanched green beans alongside. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Burst Tomatoes and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and slightly charred, is positioned as the centerpiece.
